ag.comment: USDA agricultural economics: crop production and livestock inventory (NASS QuickStats), Census of Agriculture farm counts/size and NASS Land Values survey (NASS QuickStats), farm income and wealth (ERS), and crop insurance experience (RMA Summary of Business); USDA FAS weekly Export Sales Reporting (net sales, outstanding sales, and shipments by commodity and destination country, published every Thursday); plus USGS estimated agricultural pesticide use by county (NAWQA Pesticide National Synthesis Project). County- and state-level, joinable to geo.counties / geo.state_ref via state_fips_code + county_code, to disasters (drought/storm) for yield-impact analysis, and to econ.fred_indicators for commodity-price context.

tables.comment: USDA NASS QuickStats field-crop statistics — production, area planted, area harvested, yield, condition, and progress — by county and state. Tall layout — filter statisticcat_desc for a specific measure and unit_desc for its unit; reference_period_desc is annual ('YEAR') for production/yield/area but weekly ('WEEK #nn') or monthly for condition/progress measures, so filter statisticcat_desc before comparing reference_period_desc across rows. NassQuickStatsTransformer drops the in-season vintages NASS also publishes for production/yield/area (reference_period_desc 'YEAR - AUG/SEP/OCT/NOV FORECAST' or 'YEAR - JAN/MAR/JUN/AUG/ SEP/OCT/DEC ACREAGE') so this table carries only each year's final published annual estimate for those measures, not every in-season revision. agg_level_desc carries COUNTY and STATE rows for the same commodity/year side by side, each independently summing to the true total (COUNTY rows for a state already sum to that state's STATE row, including 'OTHER (COMBINED) COUNTIES' placeholder rows — one per asd_code — for counties NASS suppresses from individual disclosure); filter to a single agg_level_desc before aggregating, since summing across levels multiplies the total. PRODUCTION additionally carries a parallel unit_desc='$' series (crop value) alongside the physical unit_desc='BU' series for the same key; filter unit_desc to one before summing — combining agg_level_desc and unit_desc unfiltered inflates a national PRODUCTION total roughly 5x. domain_desc/domaincat_desc and class_desc are further crosstab dimensions, not row-count noise — 'TOTAL'/'ALL CLASSES' is the aggregate row, everything else is a breakdown (e.g. domain_desc 'ECONOMIC CLASS', class_desc a named cultivar); filter both to 'TOTAL'/'ALL CLASSES' for a single per-geography annual figure. Likewise prodn_practice_desc/util_practice_desc distinguish irrigated-vs-not and grain-vs-silage submeasures — filter to 'ALL PRODUCTION PRACTICES'/the desired utilization for a single total. source_desc is 'SURVEY' (the continuous annual series) or 'CENSUS' (the quinquennial Census of Agriculture, years ending 2 or 7); most CENSUS rows have no SURVEY counterpart and carry commodities/geographies SURVEY doesn't cover, but where both report the identical annual total ('TOTAL'/'YEAR') for the same commodity/class/practice/ geography, NassQuickStatsTransformer drops the CENSUS duplicate so the annual series stays single-valued and comparable year over year. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code; also joinable to disasters drought/storm tables by county+year for yield-impact analysis.
tables.name: nass_crop_production

tables.comment: USDA NASS QuickStats livestock and poultry inventory head counts by county and state, annual — cattle, hogs, sheep, chickens, turkeys, etc. Fetched with statisticcat_desc=INVENTORY only, so production/marketings for animals & products are not in this table. Tall layout; use commodity_desc + class_desc for a specific animal class and unit_desc for the unit (HEAD). reference_period_desc cadence varies by series: most classes report one annual snapshot ('FIRST OF JAN'), but on-feed cattle classes report a separate row per month ('FIRST OF JAN' through 'FIRST OF DEC') — summing across reference_period_desc for those classes double-, triple-, or 12x-counts the same animals rather than adding distinct populations. Filter to a single reference_period_desc before aggregating. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code.
tables.name: nass_livestock_inventory

tables.comment: USDA NASS QuickStats farm counts and farm-size distribution — Census of Agriculture (source_desc=CENSUS, every 5 years: 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022; county- and state-level) plus the annual "Farms and Land in Farms" survey (source_desc=SURVEY, state-level only). Tall layout: filter domain_desc='AREA OPERATED' + statisticcat_desc='OPERATIONS' for farm count by acreage size class (domaincat_desc, e.g. 'AREA OPERATED: (1,000 OR MORE ACRES)'), domain_desc='ECONOMIC CLASS' for farm count by sales-value size class, or domain_desc='TOTAL' + statisticcat_desc='OPERATIONS' for the plain total farm count. statisticcat_desc='AREA OPERATED' carries acres operated (farm size in acres, not a count) under the same domain breakdowns. Also carries organic-status, financing-source, and NAICS-classification breakdowns for the same farm population — filter statisticcat_desc/domain_desc for the measure needed. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code; combine with nass_land_values (land value per acre) for farm-consolidation-vs-land-value analysis.
tables.name: nass_farm_operations

tables.comment: USDA NASS QuickStats agricultural land value and tenure statistics. The farm-consolidation-vs-land-value question this table exists for: filter source_desc='SURVEY' + statisticcat_desc='ASSET VALUE' + unit_desc='$ / ACRE' for the annual per-acre land value series (class_desc breaks it out by 'AG LAND, INCL BUILDINGS', 'CROPLAND', 'CROPLAND, IRRIGATED', 'CROPLAND, NON-IRRIGATED', 'PASTURELAND'), state-level only (agg_level_desc never COUNTY for the survey). source_desc='CENSUS' rows (every 5 years: 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022) additionally carry county-level ag-land area, farm-operation counts on that land, and landlord/tenant statistics (statisticcat_desc AREA/OPERATIONS/TENANTS) — a different, land-tenure-focused angle from nass_farm_operations' farm-population angle. Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code; combine with nass_farm_operations (farm count/size) for farm-consolidation-vs-land-value analysis.
tables.name: nass_land_values

tables.comment: USDA RMA Summary of Business — crop insurance experience by state, county, crop, insurance plan, coverage category, delivery type, and coverage level. Policies, acres, liability, premium, subsidy, indemnity, and loss ratio. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to disasters storm/drought tables by county+year for loss attribution.
tables.name: rma_crop_insurance

tables.comment: USDA RMA Cause of Loss — crop insurance experience by state, county, crop, insurance plan, coverage category, growth stage, cause of loss (peril), and month of loss. Policies, acres, liability, premium, subsidy, indemnity, and loss ratio broken out per peril (e.g. Drought, Excess Moisture/Precip/Rain, Hail, Freeze) — the field rma_crop_insurance's Summary of Business extract does not carry. Use this table, not rma_crop_insurance, to attribute indemnities to a specific cause; sum indemnity_amount across causes for a state/county/crop/year and it reconciles to rma_crop_insurance's total. Unlike rma_crop_insurance, RMA does not publish a quantity unit (quantity_type) for this file's acreage/production fields. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to disasters storm/drought tables by county+year for loss attribution.
tables.name: rma_cause_of_loss

tables.comment: USDA ERS Farm Income and Wealth Statistics by state and US total: cash receipts, government payments, production expenses, net farm income, and balance-sheet items. Tall — one row per year x state x variable. Values are generally thousands of USD (see unit_desc; some rows are Percent/Ratio/per farm). Joins to geo.state_ref via the state USPS abbreviation.
tables.name: ers_farm_income

tables.comment: USDA FSA program and conservation payments aggregated by county, program, and program year (ARC-CO, PLC, CRP, LFP, ERP, DMC, etc.). payments is the summed disbursement (USD); farms is a distinct-payee count (proxy — FSA files carry no farm/operation id). No commodity dimension exists (program is the finest grain). year is the disbursement (vintage) year; program_year is the crop/program year and differs. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips.
tables.name: fsa_commodity_payments

tables.comment: USDA FAS Export Sales Reporting (ESR) — weekly net sales, outstanding sales, shipments, and marketing-year total commitment by commodity and destination country, published every Thursday. year is the FAS marketYear (not calendar year; marketing-year start month varies by commodity — e.g. corn/soybeans start September 1, wheat starts June 1). One row per commodity x country x week_ending_date. weekly_exports is that week's physical shipments; accumulated_exports is the marketing-year-to-date shipment total; outstanding_sales is contracted-but-not-yet-shipped quantity; current_my_net_sales/current_my_total_commitment cover the active marketing year, next_my_outstanding_sales/next_my_net_sales are forward sales already booked against the following marketing year (used for early-signal detection, e.g. a large next_my_net_sales spike ahead of the current marketing year's close). country_code is FAS's own numeric code (China=5700, not an ISO code); country_iso3 carries the ISO 3166-1/GENC alpha-3 equivalent where FAS publishes one (null for FAS regional/historical groupings that are not real ISO countries) for a best-effort join to ref.countries.iso_alpha3. Detecting a purchase pause/resume: filter commodity_code + country_code and watch weekly_exports and current_my_net_sales (a net sales row can go negative on a cancellation) week over week; a sudden multi-week run of zero/near- zero weekly_exports and current_my_net_sales after a prior active run is the pause signature, a resumed positive current_my_net_sales week is the resume signature. Joins to econ.fred_indicators (commodity price context) and ag.nass_crop_production (US production side of the same commodity).
tables.name: fas_export_sales

tables.comment: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns: per-acre (field crops) or per-cwt/ per-head (milk, cow-calf, hogs) cost of production vs. gross value of production, by commodity, USDA Farm Production Region (7 regions plus a U.S. total), and year (1996-present). Tall — one row per commodity x region x year x category x item. category groups rows into gross value of production, operating costs, allocated overhead, costs listed (their sum), net value (value less total costs listed), production practices (irrigated/dryland share), and supporting information (price, yield). Covers 9 field crops (corn, cotton, barley, peanuts, rice, sorghum, oats, soybeans, wheat) and 8 livestock categories (milk, cow-calf, and 6 hog production types). Updated twice yearly (preliminary annual estimates in May, final in October). Complements ers_farm_income (farm-SECTOR aggregates) and nass_crop_production (physical production/value, no cost side) with the per-crop cost-vs-revenue breakdown neither provides.
tables.name: ers_commodity_costs_returns

tables.comment: USGS NAWQA Pesticide National Synthesis Project estimated annual agricultural pesticide use by county, active-ingredient compound, and year — low and high estimate methods (epest_low_kg / epest_high_kg, kilograms applied) for the conterminous United States, reflecting two different assumptions used when Crop Reporting District-level survey data was incomplete. Compiled from every county-level release the source currently publishes: final annual files for 1992-2012, the 2013-17 (ver 2.0) consolidated final release, and single-year preliminary releases thereafter. Preliminary years cover far fewer compounds than the finalized series — 2019 holds only 69 of the ~400 compounds present in 2013-2018 — because USGS calculates preliminary estimates as soon as data becomes available from its survey provider, ahead of the full compound set. A finalized 2018-2022 release restoring the full compound list is scheduled by USGS for December 2026 and will replace these preliminary partitions on reprocess; until then, filter to year <= 2018 for a compound set that is stable across years. Excludes seed-treatment pesticide application beginning in 2015 (the survey provider discontinued those estimates) and excludes the separate state-level-by-crop-group series (different grain, not in this table). Joins to geo.counties via the derived county_fips column and to geo.state_ref via state_fips_code.
tables.name: pesticide_use_by_county

tables.comment: UN FAO FAOSTAT production, land use, and food-balance statistics per area (country) x item x element x year. Tall — the international analog of the USDA NASS/ERS tables. country_code is the UN M49 / ISO 3166-1 numeric code (FK to ref.countries.iso_numeric); FAO regional/economic-group areas are flagged is_aggregate. Fan out one normalized bulk file per FAOSTAT domain; year is emitted per row and the partition is replaced wholesale on re-run.
tables.name: faostat_production

banking.comment: U.S. banking-sector data: FDIC-insured institution and branch registries, branch-network change history, bank failures, branch-level deposit summaries, call-report financials, and industry-wide summaries, plus CFPB consumer complaints against financial companies. Each institution/branch row carries a county_fips/state_abbr for joins to geo (states/counties), and complaint rows join to institutions/companies by name for consumer-protection research.

tables.comment: Snapshot of every FDIC-insured institution, active and inactive — charter class, chartering/regulating agency, main-office location, and total_assets_thousands / total_deposits_thousands as of the latest call report. One row per institution; PK is cert. Joins to locations, history, failures, sod, and financials by cert. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/institutions.
tables.name: institutions

tables.comment: Snapshot of every FDIC-insured institution's branch/office locations — main-office flag, service type, and geocoded address. One row per office; PK is uninum. Joins to institutions by cert and to sod (branch-level deposits) by uninum. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/locations.
tables.name: locations

tables.comment: Branch-network change events (opening / closing / acquired-in-merger, etc.) — the branch open/close/merger event log. One row per transaction; PK is transnum. Windowed by EFFYEAR (effective year of the change). Joins to institutions by cert. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/history.
tables.name: history

tables.comment: Bank failure resolutions — resolution type, deposits/assets at failure, and the acquiring institution (when any). One row per failure; PK is id. Windowed by FAILYR. cert is nullable — some very old records have no CERT. Joins to institutions by cert. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/failures.
tables.name: failures

tables.comment: Federal Reserve enforcement actions against state member banks, bank holding companies, and individuals under Fed jurisdiction — cease-and- desist orders, written agreements, civil money penalties, prohibitions from banking, and prompt corrective action notices. Board of Governors bulk CSV, full history back to 1989, refetched and overwritten in full each cycle (the source carries no per-row last-modified field, so an incremental append could miss a later-added termination_date on an already-seen row). Covers Federal Reserve-supervised entities only: OCC-regulated national banks and FDIC-regulated state non-member banks are NOT covered here, since neither publishes a bulk enforcement feed (OCC's EASearch is a search-only web form; FDIC's BankFind Suite API has no enforcement endpoint). No natural primary key: effective_date + banking_organization is not unique (the source legitimately carries multiple concurrent actions against the same organization on the same date), and there is no cert number to join against banking.institutions — individual_affiliation/banking_organization are free-text name and location strings only. Source: federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg bulk CSV.
tables.name: enforcement_actions

tables.comment: Annual branch-level deposit totals from FDIC's Summary of Deposits survey — deposits_branch_thousands per branch plus the owning institution's deposits_institution_total_thousands. One row per (branch, year); windowed by the literal YEAR field (a plain equality filter, not a range). Joins to locations by uninum and to institutions by cert. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/sod.
tables.name: sod

tables.comment: Quarterly call-report financials — total assets/liabilities, domestic deposits, net income, employee count, key ratios (equity/assets, net interest margin), CRE loan balances by property type (nonfarm-nonresidential, construction/land development, multifamily), and total risk-based capital, per institution per report date. One row per (cert, repdte). VERY LARGE (millions of rows all-history). Windowed by a REPDTE date range covering the calendar year. Joins to institutions by cert. The CRE fields let a caller compute a standard CRE-concentration ratio (CRE loans / total risk-based capital) directly, joined against institutions' charter-city geography, without relaying a third-party screener's numbers. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/financials.
tables.name: financials

tables.comment: Annual FDIC industry summary — bank count, net income, interest income, liabilities, and equity, either per-state or (when state_abbr is absent) a nationwide rollup. One row per (year, state_abbr); windowed by the literal YEAR field. Small table (~8K rows nationwide). Many fields are legitimately null in 1930s-40s records because call reports genuinely did not collect them then — real historical sparsity, not an ETL defect. Source: api.fdic.gov/banks/summary.
tables.name: summary

tables.comment: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database — one row per consumer complaint against a financial company, with product/issue taxonomy and company response. Fanned out over year x state x product (5 products) to keep each fetch unit under CFPB's 10,000-row page cap; the aggregations endpoint has no equivalent, so this is a genuine per-complaint fetch, not an aggregate. PK is complaint_id. Different host and response shape from the FDIC tables above (OpenSearch hits.hits[]._source; ISO-8601 dates). Source: consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/search/api/v1.
tables.name: consumer_complaints

tables.comment: NCUA-insured credit union branch/office locations, one row per office per quarterly cycle — main-office flag, address, and ATM/drive-thru flags. Together with banking.locations (FDIC bank branches), a UNION ALL on (state_abbr, county_name) with a literal institution_type discriminant answers any bank-vs-credit-union comparison natively. Source: ncua.gov quarterly 5300 Call Report bulk zip, "Credit Union Branch Information.txt" member.
tables.name: ncua_branch_locations

tables.comment: Community Reinvestment Act aggregate small-business lending, from FFIEC's 2024 Aggregate flat file table A1-1 ("Small Business Loans by County -- Originations"). One record per (activity_year, state, county, msa_md, census_tract, income_group_total, report_level) reporting the number and dollar volume of small-business loans originated in that geography-and- income cell across all reporting institutions, broken out by loan-size bucket (<$100k, $100k-$250k, $250k-$1M) and separately for loans made to small businesses with gross annual revenues under $1M. Grain is set by report_level: NULL rows are the tract-x-income-group subtotals, '100' rows are the county-x-income-group totals, '200' rows are the county totals across all income groups, and '210' rows are the MSA/MD totals. Loan amounts arrive in thousands of USD from the source and are carried through unchanged. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: ffiec.gov/sites/default/files/data/cra/flat-files/{yy}exp_aggr.zip (one ZIP per activity year; 2016+ zips carry the per-table member cra{year}_Aggr_A11.dat, earlier years a single combined exp_aggr.dat holding every aggregate table — CraSmallBusinessLendingTransformer handles both and filters the combined stream to A1-1 records; 116-char fixed-width record layout parsed directly by that class — see it for why this table cannot use the shared file/etl HTTP+FIXED_WIDTH path).
tables.name: cra_small_business_lending

census.comment: U.S. Census Bureau demographic and population data including American Community Survey (ACS) estimates, decennial census results, and population estimates. Provides comprehensive demographic profiles, household characteristics, income distributions, educational attainment, housing statistics, and migration patterns at national, state, and county levels.

tables.comment: State-level population summary showing total, male, and female population by year. Aggregates data from acs_population table.
tables.name: population_summary

tables.comment: State-level median household income and per capita income by year, from the ACS 5-Year acs_income table — about 2 years behind the current year. For a more current, single-year state estimate query acs1_income directly (no equivalent view exists for it yet).
tables.name: income_summary

tables.comment: State-level poverty rates calculated from poverty universe and below poverty level counts. Shows percentage of population below poverty level.
tables.name: poverty_rate

tables.comment: State-level educational attainment showing population with high school diploma, bachelor's degree, master's degree, and doctorate. Includes percentages, all as a share of pop_25_plus (population 25 and over). bachelors_rate_pct is bachelor's degree ONLY (ACS B15003_022) and excludes anyone whose highest degree is a master's, professional, or doctorate — it is NOT the "bachelor's degree or higher" rate that external benchmarks usually report. advanced_degree_pct is master's plus doctorate only (professional-school degrees, B15003_024, are not ingested). hs_rate_pct is regular high school diploma only, excluding GED/equivalency. To approximate "bachelor's or higher", use bachelors_rate_pct + advanced_degree_pct, which omits professional degrees and therefore understates the standard figure.
tables.name: education_attainment

tables.comment: State-level unemployment rates calculated from labor force and unemployed population. Shows labor force participation and unemployment percentages. Source is the ACS 5-Year survey (table B23025, via acs_employment): each row is a rolling 5-year estimate ending in "year", not a single-year annual rate, so values will differ from BLS LAUS annual or monthly unemployment rates (econ.regional_employment). Use this view for ACS-consistent comparisons with other census tables; use the econ BLS tables for the official annual rate.
tables.name: unemployment_rate

tables.comment: County-year social vulnerability profile combining ACS poverty rate (acs_poverty), senior/under-5 population share (acs_age), disability rate (acs_disability), and Spanish-limited-English-proficiency rate (acs_language) — the socioeconomic, household, and language themes of the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index. limited_english_pct covers Spanish speakers with limited English proficiency only; acs_language has no combined-language limited-English-proficiency total. Enriched with a cross-schema join to disasters.disaster_declarations for lifetime (not year-matched) declaration and Individual-Assistance counts per county, since FEMA declarations are point-in-time events that don't line up with the ACS 5-year survey vintage. One row per county per ACS 5-year vintage.
tables.name: county_vulnerability_profile

tables.comment: American Community Survey population demographics including total population, age, sex, race, and ethnicity. Provides population counts at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_population

tables.comment: Household median income and per capita income from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. A smoothed 5-year period estimate, published about 2 years behind the current year. For a more current but state-only, single-year estimate (wider margin of error) see acs1_income.
tables.name: acs_income

tables.comment: Housing unit counts, occupancy status (occupied/vacant), median home value, and median gross rent from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_housing

tables.comment: Educational attainment counts for population 25 and over from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels — population 25+, high school diploma, bachelor's degree, master's degree, and doctorate. See the education_attainment view for derived rate percentages.
tables.name: acs_education

tables.comment: Labor force status counts (civilian labor force, employed, unemployed, not in labor force) from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. Raw counts only — see the unemployment_rate view for derived unemployment and labor-force-participation percentages.
tables.name: acs_employment

tables.comment: Poverty universe (population for whom poverty status is determined) and count below poverty level from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. Raw counts only, with no demographic breakdown — see the poverty_rate view for the derived poverty percentage.
tables.name: acs_poverty

tables.comment: Decennial Census total population plus White/Black/Asian-alone race counts, at state and county levels, for census years 2000, 2010, and 2020 (every 10 years). Unified schema across all years with columns normalized to canonical names regardless of year-specific API variable codes (P001001 vs P1_001N, etc.).
tables.name: decennial_population

tables.comment: Population counts by race (White, Black, American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian, Pacific Islander, other, two-or-more) and by Hispanic/Latino origin, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_race_ethnicity

tables.comment: Median age and population counts by age bracket (under 5, 5-17, 18-64, 65+) from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_age

tables.comment: Commute mode counts (drove alone, carpooled, public transit, walked, bicycled, worked from home) and mean travel time to work, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_commuting

tables.comment: Health insurance coverage counts (with/without coverage, public, private) from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. Raw counts, not rates, and not broken out by age (age groups are summed into the totals).
tables.name: acs_health_insurance

tables.comment: Population 5+ counts by language spoken at home (English only, Spanish, Spanish with limited English proficiency, other Indo-European, Asian/Pacific Island, other), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_language

tables.comment: Population counts with any disability and by disability type (hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_disability

tables.comment: Veteran and nonveteran population counts, with a male/female veteran breakdown, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. No breakdown by period of service.
tables.name: acs_veterans

tables.comment: Civilian veterans 18 years and over broken down by period of military service (Gulf War II/post-9/11, Gulf War I, Vietnam era, Korean War, World War II, and the between-conflict gaps), from ACS table B21002, at state and county levels. Complements acs_veterans (total veteran/nonveteran counts, no period breakdown).
tables.name: acs_veterans_by_period

tables.comment: Population counts by prior-year residence (same house, moved within county, moved from a different county in the same state, moved from a different state, moved from abroad), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_migration

tables.comment: Employed civilian population counts by broad occupation category (management/business/ science/arts, service, sales/office, natural resources/construction/maintenance, production/transportation/moving), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_occupation

tables.comment: Employed civilian population counts across 13 broad industry sectors (agriculture, construction, manufacturing, trade, transportation, information, finance, professional services, education/health, arts/entertainment, other services, public administration), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_industry

tables.comment: Household counts with/without an internet subscription and with/without a computer, plus a with-broadband count (no corresponding without-broadband column), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_internet

tables.comment: Household counts by vehicle availability (no vehicle available vs. total households), from the ACS 5-Year survey table B08201 (Household Size by Vehicles Available), at state and county levels. no_vehicle_households / total_households is the standard "vehicle access" deprivation rate used alongside broadband (acs_internet) as a transportation/isolation proxy.
tables.name: acs_vehicle_access

tables.comment: Population counts by nativity and citizenship (native born, foreign born, naturalized citizen, not a citizen), from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels. native_born and foreign_born are both derived sums (B05001 has no single variable for either concept): native_born = born_in_us + born_in_pr_island_areas + born_abroad_american_parents (002+003+004), foreign_born = naturalized_citizen + not_a_citizen (005+006). The three native_born components are also exposed as their own columns — born_in_pr_island_areas in particular is analytically live on its own (most of Florida's Puerto Rico-born population), not just a summand. The full row identity is native_born + foreign_born = total_population, and at the component level born_in_us + born_in_pr_island_areas + born_abroad_american_parents + naturalized_citizen + not_a_citizen = total_population; both are DQ-asserted.
tables.name: acs_nativity

tables.comment: Marital status counts (never married, married, separated, widowed, divorced) by sex, for population 15 and over, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_marital_status

tables.comment: Household counts by type (family vs nonfamily, married-couple, single householder with no spouse, living alone) plus average household size, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_household_type

tables.comment: Occupied housing unit counts by tenure (owner-occupied vs renter-occupied), plus median home value, median gross rent, and median year structure built, from the ACS 5-Year survey, at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_housing_tenure

tables.comment: Occupied housing unit counts split by tenure (owner-occupied vs renter-occupied) and age of householder, from ACS 5-year table B25007 ("Tenure by Age of Householder"), at state and county levels. Age bands match B25007's published structure: 15-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-74, 75-84, 85+ (nine bands, identical for owners and renters). Lets a generation-cohort ownership analysis be computed directly in-engine — same age band, same vintage — rather than relying on third-party CPS reprocessing. A true generation-matched historical series still requires stitching multiple ACS vintages across the cohort's aging trajectory; this table exposes the single-vintage building block.
tables.name: acs_housing_tenure_by_age

tables.comment: Housing units bracketed by decade of structure built (ACS 5-Year table B25034), at state and county levels — ten brackets (built 2020 or later, 2010-2019, 2000-2009, 1990-1999, 1980-1989, 1970-1979, 1960-1969, 1950-1959, 1940-1949, and 1939 or earlier) plus the table's own total. Complements acs_housing_tenure's median_year_built: a median only tells you 50% of units are older/newer than itself, not the share relative to an arbitrary threshold (e.g. "percent of housing stock built before 1980") — these brackets answer that directly. Verified live 2026-09-11: bracket sum matches the table's own total exactly (Bronx County NY, 2023 ACS5); pre-1939 share is far higher in an established Northeast county (Nantucket MA ~17%) than a Sun Belt boomtown (Maricopa AZ ~1%), matching known housing-stock-age geography. Tract-grain is NOT included — this codebase's declarative ACS infrastructure has no per-county tract fan-out mechanism; state and county grain only (see all_geographies).
tables.name: acs_housing_year_built_detail

tables.comment: Household counts by ACS income bracket (under $10k through $200k+) plus total households and the Gini index of income inequality, from the ACS 5-Year survey at state and county levels.
tables.name: acs_income_distribution

tables.comment: Total, occupied, and vacant housing unit counts from the Decennial Census, at state and county levels, for census years 2000, 2010, and 2020 (every 10 years).
tables.name: decennial_housing

tables.comment: Population Estimates Program (PEP) annual population estimate (July 1 reference date), at state and county levels, for the years between decennial censuses. Data year 2019 comes from the pep/population dataset (which also includes a population density column for that year); data years >= 2020 come from the shared latest pep/charv vintage (population only, July 1 estimate; the April 1, 2020 census base is not loaded). The vintage column identifies which source dataset produced each row. One row per geography per data year.
tables.name: pep_population

tables.comment: County Business Patterns provides annual data on business establishments, employment, and payroll by industry (NAICS) at state and county levels. No sales/receipts column — for actual dollar sales by NAICS (including retail trade, naics_code '44'/'45') at county grain, see economic_census (quinquennial, not annual).
tables.name: cbp_establishments

tables.comment: ACS 1-Year population estimates (total, male, female population, median age), state level only (areas with 65,000+ population — no county breakout). More current than the 5-year table but based on a smaller annual sample, so estimates carry wider margins of error.
tables.name: acs1_population

tables.comment: Household median income and per capita income from the ACS 1-Year survey, state level plus one national row per year (areas with 65,000+ population — no county breakout). The national row has geography = 'us', name = 'United States' and a null state column; it is the Census-published national estimate, so the national median household income needs no caller-side aggregation (state medians cannot be averaged into a national median). More current than the 5-year acs_income table (about 1 year behind vs. 2), but based on a smaller annual sample, so estimates carry wider margins of error.
tables.name: acs1_income

tables.comment: Establishment counts, employment, annual payroll, and total sales/receipts (RCPTOT, in $1,000s) by NAICS industry, at state and county grain, quinquennial (2017, 2022, 2027, ...). This is the only table in the corpus with actual dollar sales/receipts broken out by industry at county level — including retail trade (naics_code '44' or '45', e.g. '44-45' combined or finer subsectors like '445' grocery/'441' motor vehicle), down to the smallest counties, so it answers "does this county's growth support retail demand" with real retail sales dollars rather than population/income/employment proxies. Uses dimension resolver to handle NAICS version differences: - 2017: Uses NAICS2017 variable - 2022: Uses NAICS2022 variable Partitioned by year only (not geography) to reduce file count. For annual (non-quinquennial) county-level establishment counts, employment, and payroll by NAICS — no sales — see cbp_establishments. For annual county-level employment and wages by NAICS — no sales — see econ.county_qcew.
tables.name: economic_census

tables.comment: Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE) annual estimates of median household income, poverty count, and poverty rate (all ages and ages 0-17), at state and county levels.
tables.name: saipe_poverty

tables.comment: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE) annual estimates of insured/uninsured population counts and insured/uninsured rates, at state and county levels.
tables.name: sahie_insurance

tables.comment: Business Dynamics Statistics annual job creation, job destruction, net job creation, establishment, firm, and employee counts, at state level. No industry or firm- characteristics breakdown in this table.
tables.name: bds_dynamics

tables.comment: Annual Business Survey (ABS) employer-firm counts, sales receipts, employee counts, and annual payroll, at state level. No owner-demographic (race, sex, veteran, education) breakdown in this table.
tables.name: abs_characteristics

tables.comment: Nonemployer Statistics establishment counts and total receipts by NAICS industry, for businesses with no paid employees (self-employed/unincorporated), at state and county levels. Physically partitioned by year only (not geography) to reduce file count.
tables.name: nonemployer_statistics

tables.comment: Building Permits Survey tracks new privately-owned residential construction permits by state. Uses December cumulative (YTD) totals. Data from https://www2.census.gov/econ/bps/State/ URL format is stYYMMy.txt where YYMM is year-month code (e.g., 2212 = Dec 2022). Partition 'period_code' stores the raw YYMM code for URL compatibility only — it is NOT a year (e.g. 2012 is Dec 2020, not 2012) and must never be filtered as one. Use the derived survey_year / survey_month columns (parsed from survey_date) for year/month filtering.
tables.name: building_permits

tables.comment: LEHD Quarterly Workforce Indicators, Sex-by-Age tabulation at state level (all industries, private ownership). One row per state x quarter x demographic cell. Ingested from the per-state bulk CSV rather than the per-quarter API: one file carries that state's whole history, so a release costs 51 fetches instead of ~4,700, and every published measure and suppression flag is retained rather than a five-variable projection. Payroll is entirely NULL (sPayroll=5) in every row as of R2021Q4 onward -- Census permanently suppressed QWI Total Payroll measures for privacy protection and redirects users to BLS QCEW instead; this is a source-side omission, not an ingestion gap.
tables.name: qwi_employment

tables.comment: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) Workplace Area Characteristics (WAC): total job counts at the workplace census block level, broken out by worker age bracket (<=29, 30-54, 55+) and by monthly earnings tier, partitioned by state and year.
tables.name: lodes_workplace

tables.comment: Median earnings in the past 12 months by sex and educational attainment, for the population 25 years and over, from the ACS 5-Year survey table B20004, state level only (no county breakout — the table is fetched with for=state:*, unlike most other acs_* tables in this schema which also carry a county grain). Reports total, male, and female median earnings (dollars) at 6 attainment levels: less than high school, high school graduate (includes equivalency), some college or associate's degree, bachelor's degree, and graduate or professional degree. Complements acs_education (population counts by attainment, no earnings) and acs_income (household income, not tied to the householder's own educational attainment).
tables.name: acs_earnings_by_education

tables.comment: Joint nativity-by-education counts for the population 25 years and over, from the ACS 5-Year survey table B06009 (Place of Birth by Educational Attainment in the United States), state level only (no county breakout). Unlike acs_nativity (population by nativity only) and acs_education (population by attainment only), this table carries the actual joint counts — e.g. foreign_born_bachelors_or_higher is the real number of foreign-born adults with a bachelor's degree or higher, not an estimate derived by assuming independence across the two separate tables.
tables.name: acs_nativity_by_education

tables.comment: Median household income and household counts by nativity of the householder (total, native, foreign born, foreign born naturalized citizen, foreign born not a citizen), from the ACS 5-Year subject table S0501 (Selected Characteristics of the Native and Foreign-Born Populations), state level only (no county breakout). S0501 classifies households by the nativity of the population column; row 089 (households_*) is the households-count denominator and row 101 (median_household_income_*) the dollar estimate, for each of the 5 nativity columns S0501 defines (C01 total, C02 native, C03 foreign born, C04 foreign born naturalized citizen, C05 foreign born not a citizen). Fetched from the acs5/subject endpoint (a different Census API dataset path than the acs5 detailed-table endpoint the other acs_* tables in this schema use).
tables.name: acs_income_by_nativity

tables.comment: Industry mix of the civilian employed population 16 years and over by nativity, from the ACS 5-Year subject table S0501 (Selected Characteristics of the Native and Foreign-Born Populations), state level only. Answers "what share of industry X's workforce is foreign-born": for each of 3 nativity groups (total, native, foreign born) S0501 reports the PERCENT of that group's employed people working in each of 13 broad industries (columns <industry>_pct_<nativity>), plus the group's employed headcount (employed_<nativity>). Workers in an industry for a group = employed_<nativity> * <industry>_pct_<nativity> / 100; the foreign-born share of an industry's workforce = employed_foreign_born * <industry>_pct_foreign_born / (employed_total * <industry>_pct_total). Percentages are published rounded to 0.1, so derived counts carry that rounding on top of the ACS sampling error. Industries are the 13 broad groups S0501 publishes (no finer NAICS detail; finer industry by nativity exists only in ACS PUMS microdata). The naturalized-citizen / non-citizen split S0501 also publishes is not carried (the Census API caps a request at 50 variables). Values are null where the Census suppresses an estimate.
tables.name: acs_industry_by_nativity

tables.comment: State-level reported voting and registration rates for the citizen voting-age population, from the Census Bureau's Current Population Survey (CPS) Voting and Registration Supplement — a biennial November survey module (even years only: congressional and presidential election years), not part of the ACS and not on the acs5 endpoint. The CPS API (api.census.gov/data/{year}/cps/voting/nov) returns person-level survey microdata (one row per respondent, with person weight PWSSWGT), not a pre-tabulated table, so this table is a weighted state-level aggregation of that microdata computed by CpsVotingSupplementTransformer: voted_rate_pct / registered_rate_pct are the population-weighted share of respondents answering "Yes" to PES1 (did you vote?) / PES2 (registered to vote?), among respondents who gave a Yes/No answer (excluding "Not in Universe", "Refused", "Don't Know"). population_reported_voted / population_reported_registered are the weighted denominators (the estimated citizen voting-age population that answered the question); sample_size_voted / sample_size_registered are the unweighted respondent counts backing each estimate, for margin-of-error context. Available biennially from 1996 (the earliest api.census.gov vintage for this dataset with PES1/PES2 variable coding stable through the most recent cycle — the November 1994 file predates api.census.gov and used different variable codes, PES3/PES4, for the same two questions, so 1994 is not in this table). CAUTION for turnout-gap or turnout-rate comparisons across states: this table is SELF-REPORTED turnout among the citizen voting-age population, known to systematically OVER-REPORT relative to actual counted votes (social-desirability bias) — it is NOT voting-eligible population (VEP), the standard denominator the turnout literature actually uses (Cantoni & Pons; McDonald/US Elections Project). For any question comparing turnout RATES between groups of states (e.g. by a policy like voter-ID requirements), prefer pairing real certified vote totals (e.g. officials.presidential_election_results or an equivalent FEC/certified- results table) with a VEP-style population denominator instead of this table's self-reported rate — this table alone will overstate turnout by roughly 10 points and can misstate a gap's size even when the direction is right.
tables.name: cps_voting_supplement

tables.comment: Work-permit (Employment Authorization Document, EAD) applications processed by USCIS, from the quarterly Form I-765 report of the Department of Homeland Security / USCIS Chief Data and Analytics Office. One row per fiscal year x fiscal quarter x EAD eligibility category x filing type. The category is the immigration basis for the permit (ead_category codes such as A03 refugee, A055 granted asylum, A124/C19 TPS, C08 pending asylum application, C09 pending adjustment of status, C26 H-4 spouse of H-1B worker, C33 DACA; ead_category_description gives the USCIS wording). filing_type is Initial, Renewal, Replacement or Not Requested. Counts are receipts (applications received in the quarter), approvals and denials (decisions made in the quarter, which may relate to applications received earlier), and pending (applications awaiting a decision at quarter end). fiscal_year is the U.S. federal fiscal year (Oct 1 - Sep 30): fiscal_quarter 1 is October-December of the previous calendar year. CAUTION: these are application FLOWS and a pending backlog, NOT counts of people currently holding a valid work permit, and one person can file more than once. There is no industry or occupation breakdown in any USCIS release; do not use this table for employment by industry. Counts are restated by USCIS in later releases. Pending cannot be reconstructed by summing quarters. Coverage starts at FY2025 (the earliest quarterly workbooks USCIS still publishes as xlsx); FY2026 Q1 is not published by USCIS and is absent. Source: https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/immigration-and-citizenship-data
tables.name: uscis_i765_employment_authorization

cftc.comment: CFTC-jurisdiction swap and derivatives transaction data, publicly disseminated from the DTCC Global Trade Repository under 17 CFR Part 43 (Dodd-Frank). Daily end-of-day cumulative files across five asset classes — rates, credit, forex, equities and commodities — carrying notional amounts, prices, effective and expiration dates, clearing status and counterparty jurisdiction. Coverage starts 2024-01-01, the post-Part-43/45 rewrite schema; earlier years use an incompatible field structure and are not included.

tables.comment: CFTC swap trade public dissemination records from DTCC GTR. Each row is one reported swap event (new trade, amendment, termination, correction). Covers all five CFTC asset classes, one per partition: RATES, CREDITS, FOREX, EQUITIES, COMMODITIES (the source short code IR/CR/FX/EQ/CO is preserved in asset_class_code). Partitioned by asset_class/year/month. Daily EOD files from 2024-01-01; weekends and holidays produce no file (skipped cleanly). trade_date is the swap's own original execution/event date, not the dissemination file's date — DTCC occasionally discloses a swap late (a handful of rows carry a pre-2024 trade_date inside a post-2024 daily file; confirmed against event_timestamp, not a parsing defect), so MIN(trade_date) can read slightly earlier than the 2024-01-01 fetch start. For new trades only: WHERE action_type = 'NEWT'. For live trades: exclude action_type IN ('TERM','CORR','EROR'). Join on dissemination_id / original_dissemination_id to reconstruct amendment chains. For a narrower, asset-class-specific column set see rate_swaps, credit_default_swaps, fx_derivatives, equity_derivatives, and commodity_derivatives; for daily aggregate summaries see swap_activity and clearing_activity.
tables.name: cftc_trades

tables.comment: CFTC Commitments of Traders — Disaggregated Futures-Only report. Weekly (Tuesday) open interest and long/short/spread positions by trader category — producer/ merchant, swap dealer, managed money, other reportables, and nonreportables — one row per (report_date, contract market). A different CFTC dataset from cftc_trades (DTCC GTR OTC swap dissemination): this is the futures-market positioning report, sourced directly from CFTC's own public Socrata endpoint (resource 72hh-3qpy), not DTCC. Series starts 2006-06-13 — the true start of the Disaggregated report, not a fetch limit (the Legacy COT report, a different resource, goes back to 1986). Source: publicreporting.cftc.gov/resource/72hh-3qpy.json.
tables.name: cot_disaggregated_futures

crime.comment: Comprehensive U.S. crime and public safety data from FBI Crime Data Explorer (CDE) and Bureau of Justice Statistics (BJS). CDE tables cover law enforcement agencies, summarized offense rates, agency-level offenses, arrests, supplementary homicide reports (SHR), police employment, hate crimes, use of force, LEOKA (officers killed/assaulted), cargo theft, human trafficking, agency participation rates, and estimated crime counts. BJS tables cover NIBRS national crime estimates, NCVS personal and household victimization, and NCVS population data. All state-level tables join with geo.state_ref via state_abbr.

tables.comment: FBI CDE law enforcement agency registry. ~19,600 agencies across 51 jurisdictions with ORI identifiers, agency type, county, NIBRS reporting status, and coordinates. One row per agency. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: cde_agencies

tables.comment: FBI CDE summarized crime rates by state and offense type. Includes offense rate, clearance rate, national comparison rates, population, and coverage percentage. One row per state + offense + month. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: cde_offenses

tables.comment: FBI CDE police employment data by state and year. Includes officers per 1,000 population, male/female officer and civilian counts, and population coverage.
tables.name: cde_police_employment

tables.comment: FBI CDE LEOKA (Law Enforcement Officers Killed and Assaulted) Police Employee data at AGENCY-year grain — one row per (ori, year) with the same total-sworn-officer and civilian counts that cde_police_employment carries at state grain, plus the county the FBI itself publishes for each ORI. Sourced to close the gap #266 identified: no table gave county-grain sworn-officer headcount over time, so a policing-intensity-vs-crime-rate analysis at county grain was structurally impossible from this schema. Roll-up: GROUP BY county_name (or JOIN cde_agencies via ori for canonical county naming and geo.counties FK linkage) collapses this to county-year. GROUP BY state_abbr recovers cde_police_employment's totals — both are LEOKA-derived, but the state-grain table pulls the CDE API's state aggregate directly while this table sums per-agency reports, so tiny differences can appear on years with late-arriving amendments between the two API paths' snapshots. **Source**: two live endpoints, chained in the DataProvider — api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde/agency/byStateAbbr/{state} gives each state's ORI list plus FBI's own county label per agency, then cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/pe/agency/{ori}?from=Y&to=Y returns that agency's PE record for the year. Confirmed live 2026-09-14 (Nome PD AK0010600 FY2020 = 9 male + 1 female officers, matching a real small Alaska department). **NULL-response filtering**: the pe/agency endpoint returns a fully-null envelope for ORIs that never reported PE data in the queried year. Those rows are dropped rather than stored as all-NULL counts — a real "no data" from LEOKA is the same as "agency did not report", not a distinguishable state worth carrying. Row count per year therefore reflects only agencies that actually reported. **County-name convention**: FBI publishes county as UPPER-CASE with hyphens ('KENAI PENINSULA'), 'NOT SPECIFIED' for state-police/university/airport/tribal agencies that don't sit in a single county, and occasional multi-county strings for agencies spanning two counties. Kept verbatim from the source; a downstream view can normalize to geo.counties.county_name (title case) via UPPER() / TRIM() plus the NOT-SPECIFIED filter. **API key**: uses API_DATA_GOV env var (same key already used by cde_agencies). The PE endpoint itself is keyless; only the agency-list call routes through api.usa.gov.
tables.name: cde_police_employment_by_agency

tables.comment: FBI CDE hate crime statistics by state and year. Flattened from nested sections (bias_section, incident_section) with categories (victim_type, offense_type, offender_race, bias, etc.) and labels with counts.
tables.name: cde_hate_crimes

tables.comment: FBI CDE use of force data by state and year, flattened into generic section/category/label rows with a single numeric value that may be a count or a percentage (see the value column). One row per state + year + section + category + label. The CDE API rejects years before 2019 outright ("Year field cannot be less than 2019"); the schema's 2010 floor is shared with every CDE table but this dataset has no years before 2019 to backfill.
tables.name: cde_use_of_force

tables.comment: FBI Return A master file: agency-level monthly counts of Part I offenses (reported/unfounded/actual/cleared/juvenile-cleared) plus officers killed and assaulted, from the CDE bulk download (one national fixed-width file per year) instead of per-ORI API calls. One row per agency (ORI7) per month, unpivoted from the wide 12-month record. Cross-references cde_agencies via ori (ORI7 prefix). Values are the FBI master file's own, unmodified. The file carries no per-month completeness flag: a month row exists for every agency-year, and an agency that did not report a month can hold 0 or a small late-adjustment count there, which is indistinguishable from a genuine low month. number_of_months_reported is a single header-level count and does not identify which months are empty, so 12 rows are not 12 reported months. Some agencies also carry a second record under the same ori (a different population_group, typically zero or small adjustments) that must be summed with the primary record. Some agencies record a whole year's counts in a single month (typically December), so month-level seasonality is unreliable; annual totals are the safer grain. The FBI revises this master file for the current and recent years as agencies file late or corrected submissions (e.g. NYPD's 2024 monthly murder counts increased after initial publication); a fixed year=YYYY.zip URL is not a stable snapshot. The month dimension below is a pure cache-buster (not present in the URL) so every calendar month re-fetches and re-materializes each year, picking up FBI-side revisions instead of freezing the ingest-time snapshot. Even the fully revised FBI total for a year can still trail an agency's own published figure (e.g. NYPD's own site), since Return A submissions lag and consolidate on the FBI's schedule, not the agency's; that residual gap is a source/methodology difference, not a defect.
tables.name: cde_reta

tables.comment: FBI CDE arrest data by state, aggregated to annual (Jan-Dec) totals for all offenses combined — the offense dimension is fixed to 'all', so individual offense categories (e.g., drug abuse, DUI, violent crime) are not broken out. Counts are broken down by age group, sex, race, and ethnicity via the section/category/label columns. One row per state + year + section + category + label.
tables.name: cde_arrests

tables.comment: FBI CDE Supplementary Homicide Report data, aggregated to annual (Jan-Dec) counts by state — not incident-level microdata. Victim and offender demographics for homicide incidents including age, sex, race, relationship, weapon, and circumstance details, flattened into section/category/label rows with a count. One row per state + year + section + category + label.
tables.name: cde_shr

tables.comment: FBI CDE Law Enforcement Officers Killed and Assaulted (LEOKA) data. Totals for officers killed (feloniously and accidentally) and assaulted in the line of duty, by state and year. The CDE API returns a null chart for every state for years before 2020; the schema's 2010 floor is shared with every CDE table but this dataset has no years before 2020 to backfill.
tables.name: cde_leoka

tables.comment: FBI CDE national crime trend percentages. Year-over-year change for major offense categories from a rolling 12-month comparison window. Single snapshot refreshed periodically (~monthly). No state dimension.
tables.name: cde_trends

tables.comment: ICE detention population by arresting agency (ICE vs. CBP) crossed with criminal-history category (Convicted Criminal, Pending Criminal Charges, Other Immigration Violator), from TRAC's (Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse, Syracuse University) "ICE Detainees" tracker. TRAC compiles this from ICE's own internal data obtained via FOIA/litigation — it is not ICE's own raw publication. Individually-hosted-but-public-domain source (university-hosted, not a government domain): re-verify if this 404s, same risk pattern as housing.opportunity_zones and housing.hud_subsidized_housing. Point-in-time snapshots, irregular cadence (roughly monthly-ish with gaps), spanning 2019-05-04 onward. One row per snapshot_date + arresting_agency + criminality.
tables.name: ice_detention_population_by_criminality

tables.comment: FBI CDE supplemental property crime data. Stolen and recovered property values by category (Firearms, Motor Vehicles, Currency, Jewelry, etc.) aggregated at the state level. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: cde_supplemental

tables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NIBRS national crime estimates from 6 SODA endpoints. Includes weighted estimates, confidence intervals, standard errors, agency counts, and population coverage for violent and property crime indicators.
tables.name: bjs_nibrs_estimates

tables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS personal victimization microdata, one row per victimization incident recorded by survey respondents, covering 2010 onward by default (start year configurable) and lagging about 2 years behind the current year. Contains 17 fields including crime/offense type codes, police notification status, weapon use, injury, offender age and sex, location (region/MSA), and person survey weight (newwgt). Use bjs_ncvs_personal_pop as the survey-respondent denominator for computing victimization rates.
tables.name: bjs_ncvs_personal

tables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS personal population data. Demographic information for all survey respondents regardless of victimization status. Includes age, sex, race, Hispanic origin, marital status, education, income. Same 2010-onward coverage and ~2-year publish lag as bjs_ncvs_personal. Used as denominator for computing victimization rates from bjs_ncvs_personal.
tables.name: bjs_ncvs_personal_pop

tables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS household victimization microdata, one row per household-level victimization incident, coded by newcrime/newoff crime and offense type codes. Includes police notification status, region/MSA, household income bracket, and household victimization weight (wgtviccy). Same 2010-onward coverage and ~2-year publish lag as bjs_ncvs_personal. Cross-references bjs_ncvs_household_pop as the denominator for household victimization rates.
tables.name: bjs_ncvs_household

tables.comment: Bureau of Justice Statistics NCVS household population data — demographic data (region, MSA, household income bracket, household size) for all participating households regardless of victimization, with household weight (wgthhcy). Same 2010-onward coverage and ~2-year publish lag as bjs_ncvs_personal. Used as the denominator for computing bjs_ncvs_household victimization rates.
tables.name: bjs_ncvs_household_pop

cyber-threat.comment: Cyber threat intelligence, exploit data, IOC feeds, MITRE ATT&CK taxonomy, and standards/compliance mappings. Part of the govdata cyber sub-domain.

tables.comment: MITRE ATT&CK enterprise-domain technique and sub-technique records, one row per technique, fetched from the enterprise-attack.json STIX2 bundle (sub-technique parent resolved via subtechnique-of relationships). Carries per-technique platforms, data sources, and detection guidance plus the ATT&CK version string; refreshed on MITRE's April/October release cadence. Mapped to NIST 800-53 controls in attack_to_nist_mappings below.
tables.name: attack_techniques

tables.comment: URLhaus (abuse.ch) malicious URL indicators, one row per reported URL, with online/offline status, threat classification, and reporter tags, partitioned by first_seen date. Snapshot re-fetched and overwritten per partition each run. See active_threat_intel below for a normalized cross-indicator view spanning ioc_urls, ioc_ips, and ioc_hashes.
tables.name: ioc_urls

tables.comment: MalwareBazaar (abuse.ch) malware sample hashes — SHA-256/SHA-1/MD5 plus ssdeep and TLSH fuzzy hashes — with file type, malware family signature, ClamAV detection name, and VirusTotal detection percentage, one row per sample, partitioned by first_seen date. See active_threat_intel below for a normalized cross-indicator view spanning ioc_hashes, ioc_urls, and ioc_ips.
tables.name: ioc_hashes

tables.comment: Feodo Tracker (abuse.ch) botnet command-and-control IP blocklist — typically ~5 active entries — with port, online/offline status, ASN, AS name, associated malware family, and geolocated country (joined to ref.countries), partitioned by first_seen date. For a broader multi-source feed that also carries ip:port indicators, see ioc_mixed (ThreatFox) below; see active_threat_intel for a normalized cross-indicator view spanning ioc_ips, ioc_urls, and ioc_hashes.
tables.name: ioc_ips

tables.comment: ThreatFox (abuse.ch) multi-type IOC feed covering ip:port, domain, url, md5_hash, and sha256_hash indicators in a single table, with malware family, threat type, confidence level (0-100), and an is_compromised (legitimate-asset) flag, partitioned by first_seen date. Requires CYBER_THREATFOX_API_KEY. Distinct source and indicator mix from the single-type ioc_ips/ioc_urls/ioc_hashes tables (Feodo/URLhaus/MalwareBazaar).
tables.name: ioc_mixed

tables.comment: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 security controls. Sourced from the usnistgov/oscal-content GitHub repository in OSCAL JSON format. Includes both base controls and enhancements (e.g., AC-2(1)). Description assembled from statement/item parts recursively.
tables.name: nist_controls

tables.comment: NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories. One row per subcategory (most granular level). 3-level hierarchy: Function → Category → Subcategory. 6 functions: GV (Govern), ID (Identify), PR (Protect), DE (Detect), RS (Respond), RC (Recover).
tables.name: nist_csf_functions

tables.comment: CIS Controls v8 safeguards from the CISecurity/ControlsAssessmentSpecification GitHub repository (RST format). 18 controls, ~153 safeguards. The transformer fetches individual RST files for each safeguard and parses title, description, asset type, security function, and implementation groups.
tables.name: cis_controls

tables.comment: OWASP Top 10 (2021) web application security risk categories, ranked 1-10, each with an overview and the pipe-delimited CWE IDs associated with that risk. One row per entry; sourced from the OWASP/Top10 GitHub repo's Markdown docs.
tables.name: owasp_top10

tables.comment: MITRE ATT&CK to NIST SP 800-53 control mappings from the center-for-threat-informed-defense/mappings-explorer GitHub repository. ATT&CK v16.1 mapped to NIST 800-53 Rev 5 enterprise domain. Records with status=non_mappable are excluded.
tables.name: attack_to_nist_mappings

tables.comment: AlienVault OTX subscribed threat-intelligence pulses (curated reports), each with targeted countries, malware families, mapped ATT&CK technique IDs, an IOC count, and TLP classification, partitioned by first_seen (date portion of created). Requires CYBER_OTX_API_KEY. Production daily runs append pulse version history into each partition (query current state via max(modified) per pulse_id); historical/DQ runs replace the partition wholesale.
tables.name: threat_pulses

cyber-vuln.comment: Cybersecurity vulnerability data. Canonical vulnerability records from NVD, active exploitation catalog from CISA KEV, CWE taxonomy, and cross-source identifier mappings. Part of the govdata cyber sub-domain.

tables.comment: MITRE Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) catalog, one row per CWE ID (e.g., CWE-79) with name, abstraction level (Class/Base/Variant/Compound), structure, status, and description. Full-catalog snapshot sourced from cwec_latest.xml.zip, refreshed weekly. Canonical dimension joined to NVD CVEs via vulnerability_cwes, to CISA KEV via kev_cwes, and to cyber_threat.owasp_top10 in the vuln_threat_chain view.
tables.name: cwe_catalog

tables.comment: NVD CVE 2.0 canonical vulnerability records, one row per CVE, partitioned by publication year and quarter. NVD's own catalog spans 1999-present (~347k CVEs total), but this table's own observedCoverage below is the source of truth for what's actually loaded here — check it rather than assuming the two match. Stores CVSS v2 and v3.1 base scores with their vector strings, plus a CVSS v4.0 base score (no v4.0 vector column), vuln_status, and pipe-delimited CWE IDs. The canonical CVE registry — see kev_catalog for the smaller subset known to be actively exploited, and vulnerability_cwes for the CVE-to-CWE junction.
tables.name: vulnerabilities

tables.comment: Junction table of CVE→CWE pairs, materialized from NVD at ingest time. One row per (cve_id, cwe_id) pair. Replaces query-time UNNEST on the pipe-delimited cwe_ids column in vulnerabilities.
tables.name: vulnerability_cwes

tables.comment: Junction table of CVE→affected CPE (vendor/product/version) pairs, materialized from NVD's configurations[].nodes[].cpeMatch[] array at ingest time. One row per (cve_id, cpe_criteria) pair. Enables per-vendor exploitation analysis (join to kev_catalog on cve_id, aggregate by vendor) that the base vulnerabilities table cannot answer alone. CPE 2.3 format: cpe:2.3:{part}:{vendor}:{product}:{version}:... part = 'a' (application), 'o' (OS), or 'h' (hardware).
tables.name: vulnerability_cpes

tables.comment: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog: one row per CVE known to be actively exploited in the wild, ~1,585 entries. Carries vendor_project, product, vulnerability_name, date_added to KEV, the FCEB remediation due_date, and a known_ransomware_use flag — no CVSS scores are included here. A curated subset of the full NVD catalog in vulnerabilities (join on cve_id); see kev_enriched or kev_cross_threat for KEV joined with NVD CVSS scores and CWE names.
tables.name: kev_catalog

tables.comment: Junction table of KEV CVE→CWE pairs, materialized from CISA KEV at ingest time. One row per (cve_id, cwe_id) pair. Replaces query-time UNNEST on the pipe-delimited cwes column in kev_catalog.
tables.name: kev_cwes

tables.comment: OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) records for open-source package ecosystems (PyPI, npm, Go, Maven, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist, Hex, Pub, CRAN), one row per OSV entry (osv_id, e.g. GHSA-xxxx, PYSEC-2021-xxx), partitioned by ecosystem and refreshed weekly. Carries severity type/score, package name and purl, and pipe-delimited alias IDs including CVE IDs where assigned — includes OSV-native entries with no CVE assignment. Not part of vuln_cross_refs, which is sourced solely from GitHub Security Advisories.
tables.name: osv_vulnerabilities

tables.comment: Cross-reference mappings from CVE identifiers to external advisory IDs, sourced solely from GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA) via the GraphQL API (single source per the one-table = one-source rule; NVD/OSV cross-refs are derived as SQL views over their own tables). Dedup key is (cve_id, external_id, external_source); external_source is 'ghsa'. APPEND LOG: the incremental delta crawl appends changed advisories each run, so this base table may hold exact-duplicate rows across runs. Query the vuln_cross_refs_unique view for one row per (cve_id, external_id, external_source).
tables.name: vuln_cross_refs

tables.comment: CISA cybersecurity advisory metadata, one row per advisory (e.g., AA24-001A, ICSA-24-001-01), partitioned by year. CISA's own feed goes back to 2017, but this table's own observedCoverage below is the source of truth for what's actually loaded here — check it rather than assuming the two match. Refreshed weekly. Carries title, published_date, severity label, pipe-delimited CVE IDs mentioned in the advisory, and a short affected_systems description. Sourced from CISA's official CSAF 2.0 JSON feed (cisagov/CSAF GitHub repo).
tables.name: advisories

disasters.comment: U.S. discrete emergency-event data: FEMA disaster declarations, Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation grant projects, NFIP flood-insurance policies and paid claims, NOAA storm events, and NIFC WFIGS wildfire perimeters. Each row is a bounded incident with a date, geographic footprint, and measurable damage — distinct from the continuous meteorological measurements in the weather schema. Enables disaster-risk analysis joined to SEC filings (state-of-incorporation exposure), econ employment, lands national forests (burned NF acreage), and FEC contributions.

tables.comment: Canonical FEMA disaster-declaration record. One row per disaster-declaration-county-program-area combination. Partitioned by fiscal year declared (fyDeclared). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to sec.filing_metadata by state for risk-disclosure research. Refreshed daily (declarations issued continuously within 24h of signature). Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/DisasterDeclarationsSummaries. WARNING when using this table as a physical-hazard-exposure proxy: incident_type = 'Biological' covers the COVID-19 major disaster declarations of March-April 2020, issued once per state as a single non-geographic nationwide event. Left in a per-county or per-state declaration count, it registers as "a disaster" for nearly every county in the country and erases the physical-hazard variation a query is usually trying to measure. Filter incident_type != 'Biological' (or inspect the distinct incident_type values directly) before using declaration counts as a hazard-exposure or disaster-frequency metric.
tables.name: disaster_declarations

tables.comment: FEMA Public Assistance grants to state/local governments and nonprofits for disaster recovery — approved project_amount, federal_share_obligated, and total_obligated (USD) per funded project worksheet. Largest dollar-value FEMA dataset; one row per project worksheet, partitioned by declaration year. Joins to disaster_declarations by disaster_number (many-to-one; not a declared FK) and to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/PublicAssistanceFundedProjectsDetails.
tables.name: public_assistance_projects

tables.comment: FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance projects (program_area: HMGP, BRIC, FMA, PDM, LPDM) — pre- and post-disaster resilience investment with project_amount, federal_share_obligated, and cost_share_percentage per project. One row per project, partitioned by program fiscal year (programFy). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to disaster_declarations by disaster_number (nullable for non-disaster BRIC/FMA programs). Source (API v4): fema.gov/api/open/v4/HazardMitigationAssistanceProjects.
tables.name: hazard_mitigation_projects

tables.comment: Paid NFIP flood-insurance claims — amount_paid_building, amount_paid_contents, and amount_paid_icc per claim, plus total_building_coverage/total_contents_coverage for exposure context. One row per claim, partitioned by year of loss. Distinct from nfip_policies (policy-term coverage/premium transactions, not realized losses). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to disaster_declarations / wildfire_perimeters by county+date overlap. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/FimaNfipClaims. DEPRECATION WARNING (confirmed live 2026-09-11, D-283): OpenFEMA has deprecated this exact endpoint - its own API response metadata states the dataset is frozen (no further updates) since 2026-06-01 and will stop being served entirely after 2026-10-15, in favor of a renamed v3 dataset ("nfip-redacted-claims-v3", FIMA prefix dropped). Migrating this table's source URL/schema to the v3 dataset before that date is a separate, tracked follow-up - incremental updates will silently stop working once the old endpoint is pulled, though history already materialized here is unaffected.
tables.name: nfip_claims

tables.comment: NFIP flood-insurance policy transactions — policy_cost, total_insurance_premium, total_building_coverage, and total_contents_coverage per policy term. One row per policy term. VERY LARGE (~74M rows all-history; several million per year). Partitioned by policy effective year. dqRowLimit caps DQ sampling; prod loads everything. Distinct from nfip_claims (realized paid losses, not premium/coverage). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and census_tract. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v2/FimaNfipPolicies.
tables.name: nfip_policies

tables.comment: FEMA's own property-level NFIP repetitive-loss aggregation — one row per structure that has ever met a Repetitive Loss (RL) or Severe Repetitive Loss (SRL) threshold (~240k rows), with total_losses (paid-claim count since 1978) and most_recent_date_of_loss per property. Ingested as the authoritative answer to "how concentrated are flood claims in properties that flood repeatedly": nfip_claims has no property/building identifier, and lat/lon (rounded to 1 decimal) or census_tract are both far too coarse to derive a per-property repeat-claim count from claims alone (many distinct properties share one rounded coordinate or tract). This table is FEMA's own property-level rollup, not a proxy. nfip_rl/nfip_srl are the insurance-claims-based categories; fma_rl/fma_srl are the separate Flood Mitigation Assistance grant-eligibility categories (see column comments for the exact thresholds) — a property can qualify under either, both, or neither pair. mitigated_indicator/insured_indicator reflect current status as of as_of_date, so a property already bought out or demolished can still appear (per FEMA's own dataset description). census_block_group is not carried here: FEMA's own file renders it in lossy scientific notation (e.g. "2.2055E+11" for a 12-digit code), destroying the digits after the leading county FIPS — county_fips (from fipsCountyCode, full precision) is the reliable location join instead. Distinct from nfip_claims (realized paid losses, one row per claim, not per property) and nfip_policies (policy-term coverage/premium transactions). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: fema.gov/api/open/v1/NfipMultipleLossProperties.
tables.name: nfip_multiple_loss_properties

tables.comment: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database — one row per storm event detail record (tornadoes, floods, hurricanes, hail, winter storms, wildfires, etc.) with event magnitude, direct/indirect deaths and injuries, and property/crop damage (damage_property, damage_crops; converted from K/M/B notation to USD). Partitioned by year, streamed from the per-year NCEI gzip CSV. Joins to geo.counties and to disaster_declarations by county+date overlap. state_fips/county_fips (D-284): NOAA's own STATE_FIPS uses 4 non-standard codes for Puerto Rico/Virgin Islands/Guam/American Samoa (99/96/98/97) instead of their real Census FIPS (72/78/66/60) — remapped so these join geo.state_ref like every other state. Confirmed live this also recovers county_fips for Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands specifically (their CZ_FIPS values are real Census municipio/district codes once paired with the corrected state code — 7,905/7,905 and 60/60 county-type rows now join geo.counties). Guam and American Samoa's CZ_FIPS values are NOT real Census codes even after the state remap (e.g. Guam's storm_events rows use "002"/"003"/"006", but geo.counties only carries a single unified "66010"; American Samoa uses "002"/"003" against geo.counties' real five-district "010"-"050") — NOAA evidently numbers these two territories' zones on its own internal scheme with no Census county-equivalent mapping. Puerto Rico has a smaller, closed variant of the same problem: 6 codes (72002/72004/72006/72008/72010/72012, 331 rows total across 2004-2008 only) are NWS PR public-zone codes NCEI stamped as CZ_TYPE='C' rather than 'Z' — interleaved with real odd-numbered municipio FIPS (72001, 72003, ...) in the same 2004-2008 window before NCEI switched to real-FIPS-only from 2009 onward. Because a zone spans multiple municipios there is no 1:1 remap that could recover a real municipio code from a zone code, so StormEventsStreamingTransformer explicitly nulls county_fips for these 6 values instead of emitting an unresolvable FIPS. A second, unrelated residual: for a small number of county-type rows in the 50 states (confirmed live: 72 in Alaska across this table's full history, 49 in Georgia isolated to Jan-2025-published rows, 1 in Louisiana), CZ_FIPS itself doesn't match any real county FIPS at all — e.g. Georgia's early-2025 batch pairs real county names like "WALKER" with CZ_FIPS values ("2", "4", "6"...) that belong to no actual Georgia county. Confirmed this is wrong in NOAA's own published file, not an artifact of this ingest. Neither residual has a crosswalk that recovers the correct FIPS from what NOAA actually published; a LEFT JOIN to geo.counties silently drops these rows, expect the gap rather than treating it as a join bug.
tables.name: storm_events

tables.comment: NIFC WFIGS Interagency wildfire perimeters — one row per fire perimeter (~39k features) with a simplified WGS84 perimeter polygon (geometry_wkt), gis_acres/incident_size_acres/final_acres burned area, fire_cause (Human / Natural / Undetermined), and point-of-origin land ownership (landowner_kind: Federal / Private / Other; landowner_category: USFS, BLM, NPS, BIA, State, Tribal, City, County, etc.) and jurisdictional_agency — enabling federal-vs-nonfederal burn comparisons directly from this table. Snapshot table with no year partition (refreshed via overwritePartitions); fire_year is derived from the fire discovery date. Coverage follows the WFIGS layer, which is complete only from fire_year 2020 (about 4k-8k perimeters a year); 2016-2019 hold a handful of features in total, so this is not a national multi-decade history. Use gis_acres, not final_acres, for burned-area totals: final_acres is set only on certified final perimeters (under 20% of rows in any year). Joins to geo.counties via county_fips (from point-of-origin FIPS) and to nfip_claims for post-fire flood exposure. Source: WFIGS_Interagency_Perimeters/FeatureServer/0.
tables.name: wildfire_perimeters
