This table carries FSA's own cumulative PSLF/TEPSLF/Limited-Waiver discharge totals (unique borrowers processed, total and average balance discharged per program) plus PSLF application throughput and portfolio-composition counts from the same combined workbook — it does NOT cover other discharge programs (borrower defense, closed school, total-and-permanent- disability) or credit-bureau-side delinquency reporting, neither of which FSA publishes in a comparably structured public file (credit-bureau reporting in particular is very unlikely to ever be publicly available — it lives inside CRA-borrower-servicer channels the government does not operate). Long/key-value grain: one row per (section, program, metric_name), not one row per borrower — FSA does not publish borrower-level discharge data. `section` is one of 'application_status' (application throughput, forms + borrowers), 'cumulative_portfolio' (PSLF-eligible borrower/balance counts and qualifying-payment-count buckets), or 'discharges' (the actual processed-discharge totals, the table's core answer to #721). `program` is 'PSLF' for the first two sections (they don't break out by program) and one of 'Combined' / 'PSLF' / 'TEPSLF' / 'Limited Waiver' for 'discharges'. `metric_name` is a normalized snake_case identifier for FSA's own row label (e.g. "Total Balance Discharged" -> total_balance_discharged); the workbook's original labels are FSA's, not reworded here. `metric_value` is always expressed in the base unit named by `metric_unit` — dollar amounts are converted from the source's "$X billion"-style strings to whole USD, never left as billions. dataset_type: snapshot — the whole table is replaced on every successful fetch (no year or period dimension; freshness: etag skips a re-fetch when FSA hasn't republished). `report_as_of_date` (last day of the covering month, parsed from the workbook's own "Cumulative Data as of Mon-end YYYY" label) is the only signal of which period a given row set covers — every row in one Iceberg snapshot shares the same value, and it advances only when FSA republishes with a newer month.
tables.name: fsa_pslf_discharge_summary

energy.comment: Comprehensive U.S. energy data from the Energy Information Administration (EIA) and Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA). Covers electricity generation and retail prices, utility operations, power plant inventory, generator capacity changes, fossil fuel production, state energy consumption, natural gas storage, petroleum stocks, crude oil imports, refinery operations, and coal mine production. All state-level tables join with geo.state_ref via state_abbr. EIA API tables use OFFSET pagination against v2 endpoints. Bulk tables (EIA-860, EIA-861, EIA-860M, EIA-814) use TEXT format with transformers that download, extract, and parse XLSX/ZIP archives.

tables.comment: EIA API v2 electric power operational data. Monthly electricity generation (thousand MWh), total fuel consumption (MMBtu), fuel consumption for electricity generation (MMBtu), cost per MMBtu, sulfur content, and ash content. Broken down by state, energy source, and sector. One row per state + energy source + sector + year-month. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr. THIS TABLE CANNOT BE SUMMED NAIVELY — it interleaves rollup rows with the leaf rows they already contain, on all three axes at once, and a SUM that ignores any of them multiplies the answer: (1) energy_source_code mixes leaves with EIA's own rollups — 'ALL', 'FOS', 'REN' and 'NUC' each already total other rows, and even some leaf-looking codes are nested (COL = BIT + SUB + LIG). Use fuel_is_rollup to pick one level. (2) sector_code likewise carries '99' = "All Sectors" alongside the individual sectors it sums; see sector_is_rollup. (3) geo_level mixes 'state', 'division' and 'national' rows — see that column. For a state's annual generation mix, filter geo_level='state' AND sector_code='99', take the ALL/FOS/REN/NUC rows, and SUM across the 12 months — there is no annual sentinel row, so a per-year figure must be summed from months. Selecting a single month's value per category instead mixes different peak months and produces parts that do not add up to the total. The state_energy_mix view does exactly this and is the intended entry point for mix questions.
tables.name: eia_electricity_generation

tables.comment: EIA API v2 retail electricity sales data, fetched at annual frequency (the source URL hardcodes frequency=annual, so price_month exists in the schema but is always null here). Average price (cents/kWh), revenue (million dollars), sales (million kWh), and customer counts by state and sector. One row per state + sector + year. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: eia_electricity_prices

tables.comment: EIA Form 861 annual electric utility survey. Covers all electric utilities, retail power marketers, and energy service providers. Fields include entity type, NERC region, service type, customer counts and sales by sector (residential, commercial, industrial, transportation), revenue, peak demand, and net generation. One row per utility + year. The transformer downloads and parses the annual ZIP archive of XLSX files from EIA. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr. To reach a utility's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on eia_utility_id = utility_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the utility's LEI/SEC CIK and its utility_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching utility_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses utilities filing under a differently-worded name.
tables.name: eia_utility_annual

tables.comment: EIA-861 utility-to-county service-territory crosswalk. One row per utility + state + county the utility reported serving in that year (a multi-state or multi-county utility has one row per county). Sourced from the "Counties_States" sheet of the Service_Territory file in the same annual EIA-861 ZIP archive that eia_utility_annual downloads (Counties_States covers the 50 states + DC; the sibling Counties_Territories sheet is out of scope, matching this schema's existing 50-states+DC convention). Does not carry a per-county customer count or sales split — EIA-861 does not publish one — so this table is a service-territory *membership* list, not a weighted allocation; see eia_electricity_demand_by_county for the county-grain demand apportionment built from it. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_utility_annual via (utility_id, report_year).
tables.name: eia_service_territory

tables.comment: Power-outage frequency and duration by electric utility: EIA-861 reliability indices SAIDI (average minutes of interruption per customer per year), SAIFI (average interruptions per customer per year) and CAIDI (average minutes to restore per interruption, = SAIDI/SAIFI). One row per utility + state + year, annual, data years 2013 onward (published with a ~3-year lag; the newest year is current-3). Sourced from the "Reliability_States" sheet of the Reliability workbook in the same annual EIA-861 ZIP archive that eia_utility_annual downloads (the Reliability_Territories sheet, covering only Puerto Rico/Guam/American Samoa, is out of scope). Each metric is reported under up to three bases: with Major Event Days (storms and other extreme events included), without Major Event Days (normal-conditions reliability), and — IEEE basis only — with loss-of-supply outages removed. Utilities report under either the IEEE 1366 standard (ieee_* columns) or their own non-IEEE standard (other_* columns); the two bases are not comparable, so they are kept in separate column groups and a utility usually fills only one group (the other is null). Reporting is voluntary for many small utilities, so coverage is partial and varies by year. Use the *_without_med columns to compare underlying grid reliability across regions and the *_with_med columns to see storm and extreme-event exposure. There is no statewide roll-up in this table; average across utilities weighting by ieee_customers/other_customers. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_utility_annual via (utility_id, report_year).
tables.name: eia_utility_reliability

tables.comment: EIA Form 860 annual electric generator inventory. One row per generator (plant + generator ID + year), sourced from BOTH the archive's "Operable" sheet and its "Retired and Canceled" sheet (2011 onward; earlier archives carry only an operable-equivalent). A generator therefore has a row in a given report_year's archive whether it was running that year or had already stopped — filter operating_status IN ('RE','CN') to isolate the latter, and read retirement_year for when it actually happened, as distinct from planned_retirement_year (a forecast made while still operating). Includes plant and utility identifiers, geographic location (state, county, city, lat/lon), NERC region, balancing authority, technology, prime mover, energy sources, capacity (nameplate, summer, winter, minimum load), ownership type, and energy storage flag. Transformer downloads and parses the annual ZIP archive from EIA. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_utility_annual via utility_id.
tables.name: eia_power_plants

tables.comment: U.S. natural gas transmission pipeline network — one row per pipeline segment (~32,900 segments nationwide), sourced from EIA and mirrored as a public ArcGIS FeatureServer under Esri's Federal_User_Community org (the layer's own listing: "checked monthly for updates"; EIA's own Energy Atlas hosting for this layer is not currently available — verified live, not the PA Department of Health's Pennsylvania-only re-clip of the same underlying EIA data found during initial research, which this table does NOT use). Confirmed nationwide via a spot-check of returned segments across Illinois, Minnesota, Arizona, Utah, Nevada, and Colorado — not just the Marcellus-region subset the PA mirror is limited to. geometry_wkt carries each segment's own WGS84 line geometry (LINESTRING or, for a small number of segments, MULTILINESTRING); length_m is EIA's own projected segment length in meters, not a WGS84-degree approximation. No county field is present at the source — join geometry_wkt against geo.counties (DuckDB ST_Intersects) for county-grain rollups, following the same spatial-join pattern as lands.county_federal_fee_land_share; see energy.county_gas_pipeline_presence for a pre-built rollup. pipeline_type is Interstate or Intrastate (EIA/PHMSA classification); status is "Operating" for every row in the live source despite the field's stated Active/Inactive/Abandoned vocabulary — a real constant, not a transform bug. A small fraction of segments (~0.2%, confirmed live) carry no geometry at all; geometry_wkt is null for those rather than the row being dropped, so segment_id stays a complete FID census.
tables.name: gas_pipelines

tables.comment: Grid interconnection queue: one row per generation or storage project that has requested connection to the U.S. transmission grid, from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's "Queued Up" dataset (Rand et al., 2026 edition, requests from 2000 through the end of 2025, CC BY 4.0), which LBNL compiles from the queue files of 7 ISO/RTOs and 50 non-ISO balancing areas (~98% of installed U.S. generating capacity; Alaska and Hawaii not covered; transmission-connected generation and storage only, no load interconnection or distribution-connected projects). ~38,200 rows: ~8,500 active, ~4,800 operational, ~24,200 withdrawn, ~670 suspended (q_status). Answers "how much new generation or storage is waiting to connect in this county, and of what type" — the forward-looking supply-side half of siting questions; county_interconnection_queue is the per-county rollup. county_fips is the project's FIRST listed county only (the source states multi-county requests keep just the first); the ~1,770 rows (~5%) whose source FIPS is blank have a null county_fips, and 22 rows sit outside the U.S. (state MX/ON/MB). mw_1/mw_2/mw_3 are the rated MW of resource type_1/type_2/type_3; a hybrid such as Solar+Battery has both mw_1 and mw_2, so total project MW is their sum, and LBNL's own published totals additionally include imputed storage MW that this file omits (active requests sum to ~1,865 GW here against ~2,061 GW in the report; the 8,513 active rows here are ~3% more than the report's 8,244, whose basis the file does not identify). 16 rows carry a negative mw_1 (-4 to -75 MW) in LBNL's own workbook and are kept as published, so SUM(mw) over a set that includes them is very slightly understated. q_id is unique only together with entity, and not even then for 135 pairs, so source_row (the row's position in the source sheet) is the only row identifier; a few q_id values were converted to dates or numbers by Excel in the source. Dates: q_date request entered queue, prop_date proposed online, on_date became operational, wd_date withdrawn, ia_date interconnection agreement signed. as_of_year is the edition's cut-off year. county holds the name as the queue wrote it and occasionally a town rather than the county (40 of 2,634 FIPS have more than one spelling); county_fips is authoritative. Snapshot table: the source is replaced wholesale each edition, not appended. SOURCE DURABILITY: emp.lbl.gov and eta.lbl.gov sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that no non-browser client passes (verified 2026-09-25: HTTP 403, cf-mitigated: challenge), so the workbook is read from the copy redistributed under CC BY 4.0 in the Zenodo deposit 10.5281/zenodo.22287832 (files are immutable per record). That deposit is a third party's replication package, pinned to the 2026 edition; a new Queued Up edition needs source.url pointed at a newer deposit. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to geo.state_ref via state (= state_abbr).
tables.name: interconnection_queue

tables.comment: EIA Form 860M generator inventory, one annual snapshot per snapshot_year. Captures planned additions and planned retirements with capacity (nameplate, summer, winter, energy storage). Transformer parses the XLSX directly. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr; joins eia_power_plants via plant_id. GRAIN — READ BEFORE AGGREGATING: this is a CUMULATIVE SNAPSHOT, not a change log. One row per generator per snapshot_year, so a single addition or retirement event REAPPEARS in every later snapshot it survives into — measured live, additions with change_year 2020-2024 appear in 1 to 6 distinct snapshot_years each. The row count therefore grows every year by construction (25,986 in 2016 to 38,359 in 2025) without any new events. SUMming nameplate_capacity_mw across snapshot_year multiplies every event by the number of snapshots it appears in: for change_type='Addition' and change_year 2020-2024 that is 746,721 MW across 18,688 rows, against 5,236 real generator-years — roughly 3.6x EIA's own published additions of ~40 GW/yr. To total real capacity change, first reduce to one row per (plant_id, generator_id, change_year) — e.g. pick the newest snapshot_year per generator with QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY plant_id, generator_id, change_year ORDER BY snapshot_year DESC) = 1 — and only then aggregate. snapshot_month is NULL on every row: only the December file is ingested, so the column carries no information and must not be used to disambiguate snapshots.
tables.name: eia_capacity_changes

tables.comment: PJM Base Residual Auction (BRA) capacity clearing prices by LDA (Locational Deliverability Area / pricing zone) and delivery year, sourced from PJM's public per-delivery-year auction-results workbook (pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm.aspx — no PJM Data Miner API key required). One row per LDA per delivery year: 'RTO' is the system-wide unconstrained zone; other LDAs (e.g. 'EMAAC', 'COMED', 'DPLSOUTH') layer a locational_price_adder on top when that zone is import-constrained. This is the actual capacity-procurement price mechanism behind PJM-region wholesale capacity costs — e.g. the RTO resource_clearing_price rose from $28.92/MW-day (2024/2025) to $269.92 (2025/2026) to $329.17 (2026/2027), a documented driver of PJM-region retail cost pressure. Currently covers only the Base Residual Auction (see auction_type); PJM's Incremental Auctions (1st/2nd/3rd IA) and other ISOs/RTOs (MISO, ERCOT, CAISO, NYISO, SPP) publish similar structured auction results and are a natural follow-on, not yet ingested (kenstott/govdata-ops#330).
tables.name: pjm_capacity_auction_prices

tables.comment: EIA API v2 petroleum crude oil production by state and month. Source is the single endpoint petroleum/crd/crpdn; fuel_type values are 'Crude Oil' or 'ANS Crude Oil' (Alaska North Slope). For natural gas production data, see eia_natural_gas_production table (separate endpoint, different units). One row per EIA area + process + year-month. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: eia_crude_oil_production

tables.comment: EIA API v2 natural gas production by state and month. Source is the separate endpoint natural-gas/prod/sum. Units are in different scale than crude oil (typically MCF or MMCF, million cubic feet). For crude oil data, see eia_crude_oil_production. One row per EIA area + process + year-month. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: eia_natural_gas_production

tables.comment: EIA API v2 State Energy Data System (SEDS). Annual energy consumption, expenditure, and price by state, sector, fuel type, and MSN (energy series code). The MSN code encodes fuel, sector, and metric in a compact 5-character string. The transformer decodes MSN values and maps them to human-readable sector, fuel_type, units, consumption_bbtu, expenditure_million, and price_per_mmbtu columns where applicable. One row per state + MSN + year. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: eia_state_energy_consumption

tables.comment: EIA API v2 weekly natural gas underground storage data. Covers working gas, base gas, total gas, injections, and withdrawals by EIA storage region (East, West, Midwest, Mountain, Pacific, South Central, Salt, Non-Salt, National). One row per region + storage type + report date. Useful for gas market signal analysis and year-over-year storage comparison.
tables.name: eia_natural_gas_storage

tables.comment: EIA API v2 weekly petroleum product stocks. Covers crude oil and refined products (gasoline, distillate, jet fuel, residual fuel, etc.) by PADD district and national totals. One row per area + product + process + report date. Supports supply disruption analysis, seasonal inventory tracking, and refinery margin signals.
tables.name: eia_petroleum_stocks

tables.comment: EIA API v2 Henry Hub Natural Gas Spot Price (series RNGWHHD), daily, in dollars per million Btu. Full history in one unpartitioned fetch (~7,500 rows since 1997-01-07, paginated via OFFSET). Pairs with eia_natural_gas_storage / weekly_gas_storage_signal to answer inventory-vs-price questions the corpus previously had no price series for at all — only the storage/inventory side existed.
tables.name: eia_natural_gas_price

tables.comment: EIA Form 814 monthly crude oil import survey. The transformer iterates all 12 monthly XLSX files for the given year (URL pattern impa{yy}{m}.xlsx where yy is 2-digit year and m is 1-based month digit) and unions them into a single partition. One row per import transaction per month (importer + origin country + entry port + receiving refinery). Includes API gravity, sulfur content, and volume in thousand barrels. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr (refinery state).
tables.name: eia_crude_oil_imports

tables.comment: EIA API v2 petroleum refinery process data in tall format. One row per EIA area + series (process_code) + year-month. Key series include crude inputs to distillation (CRDISS), operable distillation capacity (CAPACITY), and utilization rate (UTIL). Additional series cover catalytic cracking, coking, reforming, and other secondary processes. Pivoting into wide format is done via the refinery_utilization_summary view. One row per area + series_id + report year-month.
tables.name: eia_refinery_operations

tables.comment: MSHA MinesProdYearly coal mine production data (pipe-delimited CSV ZIP). The transformer downloads MinesProdYearly.zip and Mines.zip, performs an inner join on mine_id, filters to coal mines (COAL_METAL_IND = 'C'), and returns one row per mine + subunit + year. Includes mine demographics, operator/controller identity, geographic location (lat/lon, county, state), mine type and status, production volume in short tons, employee count, annual hours, labor productivity, and average seam height (underground mines). The transformer filters by the requested year dimension. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr. controller_name and operator_name are unstructured (no per-row id) — mine_id is per-mine, not per-company. ref.canonical_org_entity carries each as an already-resolved identity (eia_coal_controller_name, eia_coal_operator_name, each with an LEI when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.
tables.name: eia_coal_mines

tables.comment: NREL Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC) public electric charging station registry — one row per station. Station-level port counts by charging level (ev_dc_fast_num / ev_level1_evse_num / ev_level2_evse_num) and available connector types (ev_connector_types, comma-separated — e.g. CHADEMO, J1772, J1772COMBO, TESLA). Does not model AFDC's per-charger connector/power breakdown (ev_charging_units) — deeper than any known query needs; the station-level aggregate counts and connector list answer "how much charging capacity exists where." Whole registry re-fetched and overwritten each run when Last-Modified changes (confirmed live: ~90K electric stations, 200-row page cap). Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Source: developer.nlr.gov (NREL's API host as of the 29 May 2026 migration off the retired developer.nrel.gov domain; confirmed live).
tables.name: ev_charging_stations

tables.comment: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) Table 10a upstream drilling activity — active rig count, new wells drilled, new wells completed, and drilled-but- uncompleted (DUC) well inventory, monthly, for the 6 regions STEO covers (Permian, Bakken, Eagle Ford, Appalachia, Haynesville, and Rest of Lower 48 excluding Gulf of America). This is the successor to EIA's standalone Drilling Productivity Report, folded into STEO as Table 10a in June 2024 (confirmed live: full 2013-01 through present history, 24 series, ~3,900 rows, one request). Rig counts/wells drilled lead crude and gas production by months, which energy's production/capacity tables alone cannot show. One row per (region, metric, period). Whole series set re-fetched and overwritten each run when content changes.
tables.name: eia_drilling_activity

environment.comment: U.S. environmental data spanning air quality (EPA AQS monitored concentrations and AQI), toxics and greenhouse-gas emissions (EPA TRI and GHGRP by facility), surface water (USGS streamflow and monitoring sites) and county-level water-use withdrawals by sector (USGS water_use_county, 2015 census), public drinking-water systems (EPA SDWIS), and the EPA facility registry with compliance and enforcement history (ECHO/FRS). Each row is a place-and-period observation or a facility record joinable to geo (states/counties), sec (regulated companies), econ, and weather. Together they describe environmental quality, pollution sources, water availability/use, and regulatory status across the United States.

tables.comment: EPA AirData annual-summary air quality — arithmetic mean concentration, peak value, observation count, and valid-day count for PM2.5, Ozone, SO2, NO2, and CO. Source file is one row per monitor per pollutant per year, but no monitor/site id is retained here (only state_fips/county_fips), and the annual file carries no AQI column, so aqi is always null here — for AQI use air_quality_daily, which is also site-level. Keyless national bulk file annual_conc_by_monitor_<year>.zip. Moved here from the weather schema. Joins geo.state_ref via state_fips and geo.counties via county_fips.
tables.name: air_quality_annual

tables.comment: EPA AirData daily-summary air quality by monitoring site — one row per site per day per pollutant standard, with mean concentration, peak value, AQI, and observation count (plus site lat/lon). Unlike air_quality_annual (county-level, no AQI), this table retains site_number and a real AQI value. Keyless national bulk files daily_<param>_<year>.zip, one per pollutant-year. Moved here from the weather schema. Joins geo.state_ref/geo.counties.
tables.name: air_quality_daily

tables.comment: EPA AQS monitor metadata — one row per (site, parameter) with location (lat/lon, local site name, city, CBSA name), monitor type, monitoring networks, and operating span (first_year through last_sample_date). Keyless reference file aqs_monitors.zip. Snapshot; joins air_quality_daily by site and geo by county_fips.
tables.name: aqs_monitors

tables.comment: EPA Toxics Release Inventory — one row per facility × chemical × year, with release amounts by pathway (fugitive air, stack air, surface water) plus on-site, off-site, and total release totals, primary NAICS, and facility location (city, county, state, zip, lat/lon). Per-year national bulk CSV (efservice mv_tri_basic_download). Delta by year. Joins geo via state_abbr + county name; frs_id links epa_facilities.
tables.name: tri_releases

tables.comment: EPA GHGRP facility dimension — one row per reporting facility per year with location (city, state, county, zip, lat/lon), NAICS code, parent company, reported industry types, and facility type (e.g. 'Direct Emitter'). Envirofacts efservice full-year CSV. Delta by year. Join ghg_emissions on (facility_id, year) for the emissions themselves; frs_id links epa_facilities. parent_company is unstructured (no per-row id — facility_id is per-facility, not per-parent-company). ref.canonical_org_entity carries it as an already-resolved identity (ghg_parent_company_name, with an LEI/SEC CIK when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.
tables.name: ghg_facilities

tables.comment: EPA GHGRP emissions facts — CO2-equivalent emissions keyed by facility × year × sector × subsector × gas. Envirofacts efservice full-year CSV. Delta by year. Per-facility annual total = SUM(co2e_emission) over the facility-year; join ghg_facilities on (facility_id, year) for geography.
tables.name: ghg_emissions

tables.comment: EPA eGRID (Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database) regional emission rates — one row per eGRID subregion per year (~27 subregions, e.g. RFCE, CAMX, ERCT), with annual net/nonbaseload generation, total NOx/SO2/CO2/CO2e emissions, overall output emission rates (lb/MWh, all fuels combined), and per-fuel-type output emission rates for NOx/SO2/CO2 broken out by coal, oil, gas, and fossil-fuel-total (also lb/MWh), plus each fuel's share of subregion generation (coal/oil/gas/nuclear/hydro/ renewables generation_pct). This is the SRL (subregion) tab of eGRID's multi-tab XLSX workbook — the workbook also carries UNT/GEN/PLNT (unit/generator/plant-level) and ST/BA/NRL/US (state/balancing-authority/NERC-region/national) tabs; none of those have this fuel-type breakdown (plant-level rates are for the whole plant, dominated by its single primary fuel) and none are in this table. EPA publishes eGRID roughly every 1-2 years, historically each January of year+2 (eGRID2023, released 2025-01 and revised 2025-06, covers 2023 generation/emissions). The download URL is unpredictable — it embeds a publish date and a revision suffix that both vary by year and are not derivable from the data year — so this transformer discovers the year's workbook link by scraping EPA's historical-egrid-data listing page, falling back to download-data for the most-recently-released vintage (not yet moved to the historical archive at build time, 2026-08-02, eGRID2023 was download-data-only). A year with no discoverable link yields zero rows for that year, not an error — check the ETL log for "no data workbook link found" to distinguish "not published this way" from a real failure.
tables.name: egrid_emission_rates

tables.comment: USGS NWIS surface-water monitoring sites — one row per active stream site with location, HUC, and drainage area. Fetched per state from the NWIS site service (RDB, expanded output). Snapshot. site_no joins streamflow; state_fips/county_fips join geo.
tables.name: water_sites

tables.comment: USGS NWIS daily streamflow — one row per (site, date) with discharge (cfs) and gage height (ft). Fetched per (state, year) from the NWIS daily-values service (RDB; concatenated per-site blocks with dynamically-named value columns, normalized by the transformer). Delta by year; current year is re-fetched. site_no joins water_sites.
tables.name: streamflow

tables.comment: USGS county-level water withdrawals by sector — public supply, domestic, industrial, irrigation, mining, and thermoelectric power, plus an all-sector total — split into groundwater/surface-water freshwater withdrawal (Mgal/d) and, where the sector reports a saline component, total withdrawal including saline. A proxy for whether a county has spare water-withdrawal capacity for a new industrial user: compare a target sector's historical draw against the county's total. Quinquennial census (2000, 2005, 2010, 2015 — the last county-grain vintage published; USGS moved to an annual/HUC12/model-based approach after 2015). Livestock and aquaculture are omitted: their sector-code assignment is ambiguous before 2005 and immaterial to industrial-siting screening. state_fips/ county_fips join geo.
tables.name: water_withdrawals

tables.comment: EPA SDWIS public water systems — one row per active public water system (PWS) with type (CWS/NTNCWS/TNCWS), population served, service connections count, owner type, and primary source-water type (ground vs. surface). Envirofacts efservice full-state CSV (active systems only). Snapshot. pwsid joins drinking_water_violations; state_abbr joins geo.state_ref.
tables.name: drinking_water

tables.comment: EPA ECHO Exporter — one row per regulated facility (~3.2M) with registry identity, location (address, lat/lon, NAICS/SIC codes — naics_codes is backfilled from sic_codes for some SIC-only facilities, see naics_codes_derived), and a rolled-up compliance/enforcement summary: inspection count and last-inspection date, formal enforcement action count, total penalties, significant-noncompliance flag, overall plus per-statute (CAA/CWA/RCRA/SDWA) compliance status, and violation-frequency rollups — quarters (of the last 12) in noncompliance overall and per statute (CAA/CWA/RCRA), plus the CWA effluent-limit exceedance count over the last 13 quarters (null when none). Keyless weekly-snapshot bulk zip. registry_id links TRI/GHGRP frs_id; the facility_compliance view projects the compliance subset.
tables.name: epa_facilities

tables.comment: EPA SDWIS drinking-water violations — one row per violation per public water system, with violation type/category (MR=monitoring, MCL, TT, ...), health-based and major-violation indicators, contaminant code, measured value, and compliance period. Envirofacts efservice full-state CSV, filtered by primacy_agency_code (the state column; the literal `state` column silently no-ops). Snapshot. pwsid joins drinking_water.
tables.name: drinking_water_violations

tables.comment: EPA SEMS Superfund sites — one row per site (national, ~55K) with site name, street address, National Priorities List status (npl_status_code 'F' = Final NPL), federal-facility indicator, and location (county_fips, state_abbr, lat/lon). Envirofacts efservice full table. Snapshot.
tables.name: superfund_sites

tables.comment: EPA RCRAInfo hazardous-waste handlers — one row per current handler, with generator status and activity flags (transporter, treatment/storage/ disposal, recycler) plus location (city, county_code, zip, lat/lon). Envirofacts efservice full-state CSV filtered to current_record='Y' (the source table is multi-cycle history). Snapshot. Joins geo.state_ref via state_abbr.
tables.name: rcra_facilities

tables.comment: USGS/EPA Water Quality Portal — measured water-quality sample results (nitrate, metals, bacteria, pH, etc.) at monitoring locations. Fetched per (state FIPS, year) from the Result service. Delta by year; large/slow, so DQ samples via dqRowLimit. monitoring_location_id joins USGS/STORET sites.
tables.name: water_quality_samples

tables.comment: USGS county-level water-use census for 2015 (usco2015v2.0.csv, USGS data release https://doi.org/10.5066/F7TB15V5, cited in USGS Circular 1441) — one row per county (3,223 counties/county-equivalents, all 50 states + DC/PR/USVI). Reports total population and, per sector (public supply, self-supplied domestic, industrial, irrigation, livestock, aquaculture, mining, thermoelectric power), withdrawals in million gallons per day (Mgal/d) broken out by groundwater/surface-water and, where applicable, fresh/saline; thermoelectric is further split into once-through vs. recirculating cooling with power generated (GWh) and consumptive use. total_withdrawals_mgd/total_fresh_groundwater_mgd/total_fresh_surfacewater_mgd/ total_saline_withdrawals_mgd are cross-sector sums; total_consumptive_use_partial_mgd covers only irrigation + thermoelectric (the only sectors USGS estimates consumptive use for in this release) — not a full-sector total, per USGS's own "Partial" naming. Verified live 2026-09-21: summing total_withdrawals_mgd nationally gives 321.7 Bgal/d, matching USGS Circular 1441's published 322 Bgal/d 2015 total; Monroe County, MI (DTE's Monroe coal plant, Lake Erie once-through cooling) shows 1,791 Mgal/d thermoelectric withdrawal and 25,252 GWh generated, consistent with that plant's known ~3,400 MW nameplate capacity. IMPORTANT CAVEAT — this is a WITHDRAWAL-CAPACITY proxy for "does this county have a track record of sector water use," not a legal water-rights/allocation record: it does not show unallocated headroom, permitted-but- unused rights, or legal availability under drought curtailment. USGS publishes this compilation once every 5 years (Circulars 1950-2015 then per-category ScienceBase releases from 2020); this table currently holds only the 2015 vintage — the last year published as one combined all-sector county file — see the dataset_type note above for why later vintages are not mechanically addable. Joins geo.state_ref via state_fips and geo.counties via county_fips.
tables.name: water_use_county

fec.comment: Federal Election Commission campaign finance data. Contains candidate and committee registrations, itemized contributions, expenditures, and inter-committee transfers. Covers all federal elections (President, Senate, House) with data from 1980 to present. Bulk downloads are pipe-delimited files with no headers.

tables.comment: All federal candidates registered with the FEC. Includes candidate ID, name, party, office sought, state, district, incumbent/challenger status, and principal campaign committee. One record per candidate per election cycle. Source: cn{YY}.zip bulk download (pipe-delimited, no header).
tables.name: candidates

tables.comment: All political committees registered with the FEC. Includes PACs, party committees, campaign committees, and Super PACs. Contains committee type, designation, connected organization, treasurer, and filing frequency. Source: cm{YY}.zip bulk download (pipe-delimited, no header). To reach a committee's connected organization FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on fec_committee_id = committee_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the org's LEI/SEC CIK and its committee_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching connected_org_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses orgs filing under a differently-worded name.
tables.name: committees

tables.comment: Links between candidates and their authorized committees. Shows which committees are authorized by which candidates, including the linkage type and election year context. Source: ccl{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header).
tables.name: candidate_committee_linkages

tables.comment: Itemized individual (donor-level) contributions to federal committees exceeding $200 per cycle. transaction_type spans both ordinary contributions (15/15E/22Y) AND code 10 (giving to Super PACs/Hybrid PACs/nonfederal soft-money accounts) — 10 is uncapped and by dollar volume is typically the single largest code (2024: $6.2B vs. $3.6B for 15), so a query that only knows 15/15E/22Y silently undercounts total giving, especially per-donor. See the transaction_type column comment for the full code list. Largest FEC dataset (~4-5GB per cycle, 20M+ records); contains donor name, employer, occupation, amount, date, and memo text (vectorized for inferred relationship discovery). Distinct from committee_contributions (committee-to-candidate money) and intercommittee_transactions (committee-to-committee transfers). Source: indiv{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the RECIPIENT committee (join fec.committees on committee_id + year for its details) and contributor_name is genuinely the donor (individual) here — unlike committee_contributions/intercommittee_transactions, this table's column names match their roles. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition first — this is the largest FEC table by row count and an unfiltered or non-partition-filtered aggregate can exceed a 30s query timeout. Donor-name lookup ("what has this person given") is NOT currently supported even with a year filter: contributor_name has no sort order/clustering, so a name-filtered scan of one year's partition (tens of millions of rows) still exceeds the 30s statement timeout in production — confirmed 2026-09-29 (see kenstott/govdata-ops#780). Do not attempt a name-filtered query against this table until #780's remediation (a donor-summary table or sortOrder+ reprocess) lands.
tables.name: individual_contributions

tables.comment: Committee-to-candidate transactions (PACs, party committees), spanning direct contributions and coordinated/independent spending via transaction_type codes (24K=direct contribution, 24C=coordinated party expenditure, 24E=independent for, 24A=independent against, 24F=communication cost for). Each row carries a candidate_id, distinguishing it from intercommittee_transactions (committee-to-committee transfers with no candidate link). Source: pas2{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the DONOR/filing committee (the PAC or party committee that made this expenditure — join fec.committees on committee_id + year for its name/type/connected organization); contributor_name and other_id both identify the RECIPIENT (candidate's authorized committee) — contributor_name is its name despite the field's name, other_id is its FEC committee ID (join fec.committees on other_id + year for the recipient's own details), and candidate_id is the recipient candidate. amount is signed per transaction_type — a negative value is a refund/adjustment against a prior contribution, not new money moving; net (don't just sum) amount when computing a total given/received. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition — an aggregate filtered only by candidate_id (or any other non-partition column) across all years can exceed a 30s query timeout.
tables.name: committee_contributions

tables.comment: Transactions between political committees — transfers, joint fundraising allocations, and other inter-committee financial activity — with no candidate_id column, unlike committee_contributions (which links each row to a specific candidate). Shows the flow of money between PACs, party committees, and campaign committees. Source: oth{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header). DIRECTION: committee_id is the FILING committee (whose oth-schedule report this row came from) and is constant across every row for one filer; entity_type, contributor_name, and other_id together describe the COUNTERPARTY committee/entity for that one transaction (entity_type/contributor_name vary row to row even though committee_id doesn't — join fec.committees on other_id + year for the counterparty's details). Unlike committee_contributions, whether money moved INTO or OUT OF the filing committee is NOT fixed by column position — it depends on transaction_type (see FEC Schedule L code descriptions); amount is signed (negative = refund/reversal) regardless. PERFORMANCE: always filter on the year partition first.
tables.name: intercommittee_transactions

tables.comment: Itemized operating expenditures by political committees. Shows how committees spend their money — consultants, media buys, travel, rent, staffing, etc. Purpose text is vectorized for spending pattern analysis. Source: oppexp{YY}.zip (pipe-delimited, no header).
tables.name: operating_expenditures

tables.comment: Independent expenditures — spending by committees and individuals for or against candidates that is not coordinated with the candidate's campaign. Includes Super PAC spending. Source: independent_expenditure_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers). FEC accepts filings without amount-plausibility vetting, so the bulk file carries spam/prank line items of $50M to $10B (e.g. 2022 and 2024 candidates filing $9,999,999,999-scale "expenditures"); a raw SUM(amount) is inflated roughly 10x to 23x in 2022, 2024 and 2026. Every row is kept and amount is never altered; amount_implausible marks the rows to exclude. Any total, ranking or per-candidate aggregate of amount must filter WHERE amount_implausible IS NOT TRUE. A filer amending a filing resubmits the whole thing under a new file_num (amendment_indicator A1/A2/A3, prev_file_num naming the file_num it replaces) rather than correcting it in place, so the superseded filing's rows stay in this table alongside the amendment — use the independent_expenditures_current view (superseded_by_amendment) to exclude them from a SUM/count.
tables.name: independent_expenditures

tables.comment: Electioneering communications — broadcast, cable, or satellite ads that mention a federal candidate within 30 days of a primary or 60 days of a general election. Carries the reported disbursement amount plus, when one ad buy names multiple candidates, number_of_candidates and calculated_candidate_share to apportion the cost per candidate. Source: ElectioneeringComm_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers).
tables.name: electioneering_communications

tables.comment: Communication costs reported by corporations and labor organizations for internal communications (to employees, members) mentioning federal candidates, with a support_oppose (S/O) flag per candidate. Distinct from electioneering_communications, which covers public broadcast/cable/satellite ads rather than internal member communications. Source: CommunicationCosts_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers).
tables.name: communication_costs

tables.comment: Aggregated per-candidate financial summary for each election cycle — one row per candidate, not a transaction. Includes total receipts, disbursements, cash on hand, debts, and individual contributions split into itemized (>$200) vs unitemized (<=$200), plus party/other-committee contribution totals. Rolls up the transaction-level individual_contributions and committee_contributions tables rather than replacing them. Source: candidate_summary_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers).
tables.name: candidate_summaries

tables.comment: Aggregated per-committee financial summary for each election cycle — one row per committee, not a transaction. Includes total receipts, disbursements, cash on hand, debts, independent expenditures, party coordinated expenditures, and the nonfederal (non-election-account) share of transfers and expenditures. Rolls up the transaction-level committee_contributions and intercommittee_transactions tables rather than replacing them. Party affiliation and connected organization are not in this file; join to committees on committee_id for them. Source: committee_summary_{YYYY}.csv (CSV with headers).
tables.name: committee_summaries

tables.comment: Itemized contributions received by California state candidates, parties, and ballot-measure committees (Cal-Access Form 401/460/465 Schedule A/C/I), including intermediary/conduit and loan-interest detail. One row per contribution line item; PK is (filing_id, amend_id, line_item, form_type) — an intermediary contribution files a companion record (form_type I) alongside its underlying contribution (form_type A) sharing the same filing_id/amend_id/line_item, so form_type is required to disambiguate. rec_type is 'RCPT' for the vast majority of rows but a real minority (~0.006%) are 'E530' — Form 497 24-hour/10-day late contribution reports, co-mingled into the same TSV by the source. Source: Cal-Access full-database export, RCPT_CD.TSV member. Covers 2000-present. A small number of source rows (<0.001%) have a NULL filing_id/amend_id/line_item — a known Cal-Access export data-quality gap, not a transform defect.
tables.name: ca_contributions

tables.comment: Itemized expenditures by California state candidates, parties, and ballot-measure committees (Cal-Access Form 401/460/465 Schedule D/E). One row per expenditure line item; PK is (filing_id, amend_id, line_item, form_type) — Schedule D (subvendor/agent detail, form_type D) files a companion record alongside its Schedule E parent (form_type E) sharing the same filing_id/amend_id/line_item, so form_type is required to disambiguate. Source: Cal-Access full-database export, EXPN_CD.TSV member. Covers 2000-present. A small number of source rows (<0.001%) have a NULL filing_id/amend_id/line_item — a known Cal-Access export data-quality gap, not a transform defect.
tables.name: ca_expenditures

tables.comment: California Form 496 "24/48-hour" late independent-expenditure reports — the state's closest counterpart to FEC independent_expenditures / the "dark money" IE disclosure this gap was filed for. One row per IE line item; PK is (filing_id, amend_id, line_item). Unlike ca_contributions/ca_expenditures, Form 496 carries no denormalized committee/candidate/race columns in the source file itself (entity_type is always NULL here — S496_CD has no ENTITY_CD column) — resolve the spender/target via the CVR cover page (not yet sourced) or the filing_id. Source: Cal-Access full-database export, S496_CD.TSV member. Covers 2000-present.
tables.name: ca_independent_expenditures

tables.comment: California Cal-Access filer registry — every registered filer (candidate, committee, party, ballot-measure committee, lobbyist client, etc.), one row per filer-name/status record. filer_id is the join key to ca_contributions.committee_id and ca_expenditures.committee_id. Source: Cal-Access full-database export, FILERNAME_CD.TSV member. Not a strict 1-row-per-filer table — a filer with a name or status change over time carries multiple rows (xref_filer_id + effective_date vary). A small number of source rows (<0.01%) have a NULL xref_filer_id/filer_id — a known Cal-Access export data-quality gap, not a transform defect.
tables.name: ca_filers

fedregister.comment: U.S. Federal Register documents from govinfo.gov bulk XML archives. Covers final rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents (executive orders, proclamations, memoranda), partitioned by publication year and month from 2010 to present by default (start year configurable via GOVDATA_START_YEAR). Key cross-reference fields: cfr_references (links to affected CFR titles/parts by industry), rin (Regulatory Identifier Number — tracks rulemaking lifecycle from NPRM to final rule), docket_ids (links to regulations.gov comment dockets). Three tables in this schema: fr_documents (full document metadata from govinfo.gov bulk XML), fr_document_text (summary and body text of each document, from the same XML) and fr_significance (OIRA EO 12866 economic-significance flag per document, sourced directly from the Federal Register API's own JSON field — join to fr_documents on document_number). See each table for its full column list.

tables.comment: All Federal Register documents partitioned by publication year and month. RULE=final rules (binding, amend CFR), PRORULE=proposed rules (open for comment), NOTICE=agency announcements/meetings/grants, PRESDOC=executive orders/proclamations. Key analytical fields: rin (tracks NPRM→final rule lifecycle via RIN cross-reference), cfr_references (JSON: affected CFR titles and parts → maps to regulated industry), docket_ids (JSON: links to regulations.gov for comment letter intelligence).
tables.name: fr_documents

tables.comment: Text of each Federal Register document, one row per document_number (joins to fr_documents). summary is the preamble SUMMARY paragraph (a few hundred characters, the agency's own statement of what the document does); body_text is the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section of a rule, proposed rule or notice — background, discussion, the agency's reasoning and responses to comments, usually thousands of characters and up to about a million for the largest rules — and the whole text of a presidential document (executive order, proclamation, memorandum), which has no such section. The regulatory text itself (amendatory instructions and CFR text) is part of body_text when the XML places it inside SUPLINF. summary is NULL for documents without a SUMMARY (most presidential documents); body_text is NULL for the few documents with no body element. Use this table for text search; use fr_documents for title, agency, CFR references, RIN and dates.
tables.name: fr_document_text

tables.comment: OIRA EO 12866 economic-significance determination per Federal Register document, sourced directly from the Federal Register API's own `significant` JSON field (https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json) — not present in fr_documents' govinfo.gov bulk-XML source. true = economically significant under EO 12866 (subject to OMB/OIRA regulatory review), false = not significant. NULL is overwhelmingly "significance does not apply to this document type" (confirmed live: 817 of 818 Notices in a March 2026 sample are NULL, since EO 12866 review applies only to Rules) rather than "not yet classified" — filter to type='Rule' or 'Proposed Rule' before treating a NULL as meaningful. Join to fr_documents on document_number to filter significant vs. routine rules.
tables.name: fr_significance

fiscal.comment: U.S. federal fiscal data: the revenue side (IRS Statistics of Income — income, deductions and tax by ZIP, county, and taxpayer class; county-to-county migration of returns; the roster and financials of tax-exempt organizations) and the outlay side (USAspending obligations by awarding agency and by recipient state; SBA 7(a) and 504 loan approvals). Each row is a geography-and-period or entity-and-period observation joinable to geo (states/counties) and, for nonprofits and borrowers, by EIN/name. Together they show where federal money comes from and where it goes, comparable per county against population and income.

tables.comment: IRS Statistics of Income individual income tax statistics aggregated by ZIP x AGI size class (agi_stub) x tax year. The finest-grained revenue table; joins to geo ZIP crosswalks for county/CBSA rollups and to census ACS income. All dollar amounts are in THOUSANDS of dollars and may be negative. agi_stub brackets: 1=$1-25k, 2=$25-50k, 3=$50-75k, 4=$75-100k, 5=$100-200k, 6=$200k+. zip_code = 00000 rows are the state total for that state (kept; exclude in views that sum ZIPs). Source (per year): irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/{YY}zpallagi.csv.
tables.name: soi_income_by_zip

tables.comment: IRS SOI individual income tax statistics at county grain x AGI size class x tax year (coarser than ZIP, longer history). Joins directly to geo.counties via county_fips. Amounts in $1000s. county_fips ending in 000 (COUNTYFIPS = 000) is the state total (kept; exclude in views that sum counties). Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/{YY}incyallagi.csv.
tables.name: soi_income_by_county

tables.comment: IRS SOI Table 1-5, "Gross Collections, by Type of Tax and State" — one row per state/area per fiscal year, wide across the 11 tax-collection measures the table publishes. Sourced to close the gap federal_spending_vs_income_tax_by_state_year documents explicitly: that table carries individual income tax only, so a balance-of-payments computation built from it alone makes every state look net-positive (confirmed against the NY State Comptroller's official FFY2023 report, whose Rockefeller/OMB methodology finds NJ/MA/WA as real net donors). business_income_taxes (corporate) and excise_taxes here close the biggest part of that gap. **Structural IRS limitation — cannot be fixed at ETL time**: IRS combines FICA with individual income tax withheld (individual_withheld_and_fica_tax), and SECA with individual income tax payments (individual_payments_and_seca_tax), in this state-level report. A clean payroll/FICA-only-by-state figure is not obtainable from any IRS SOI state-grain publication — this is the same reason federal_spending_vs_income_tax_by_state_year never carried it. The combined columns are still the correct denominator for a balance-of-payments computation (each captures both components), just not separable into payroll-tax-alone. Non-state rows are kept, not dropped, matching soi_income_by_county's kept county-total convention: 'United States, total' (the national aggregate) and three non-state buckets IRS reports separately ('U.S. Armed Service members overseas and Territories other than Puerto Rico', 'Puerto Rico', 'International', 'Undistributed') all get state_abbr NULL — filter WHERE state_abbr IS NOT NULL for a clean 50+DC sum. Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/{YY}dbs01t05co.xlsx (FY2019-2024 combined tax-type workbook; sheet name and filename convention both changed for FY2025 — see the source block). Scoped to FY2019+ (this modern combined-workbook format) rather than IRS's full history back to the 1990s — pre-2019 files are the legacy .xls binary format with a plausibly different layout, unverified and out of scope here.
tables.name: irs_gross_collections_by_state_year

tables.comment: IRS SOI county-to-county migration derived from year-over-year address changes on returns. One row per origin->destination county for the filing year (from the OUTFLOW file: Y1 = origin, Y2 = destination). Summary/foreign buckets (state FIPS >= 57; county 000) and non-migrant same-county rows are filtered out; suppressed cells (n1 < 0) dropped. Both endpoints join to geo.counties. agi in $1000s. Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/countyoutflow{YYZZ}.csv.
tables.name: county_migration_flows

tables.comment: IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File — the roster of all registered tax-exempt entities (EIN, name, location, subsection, deductibility, NTEE, latest financials). Cumulative monthly snapshot sharded across four regional files (eo1..eo4), fetched and concatenated in one pass. subsection_code 03 = 501(c)(3); ruling_date/tax_period are YYYYMM. Anchors exempt_org_990 on EIN. Dollar amounts fold the sign into the value. Source: irs.gov/pub/irs-soi/eo{1..4}.csv. To reach this org's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on exempt_org_ein = ein — EIN is a second exact-match hub key alongside GLEIF's LEI (sec.filing_metadata.irs_number matches it directly), so the join is exact. Matching org_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses orgs filing under a differently-worded name.
tables.name: exempt_org_master

tables.comment: Nonprofit/tax-exempt financials from IRS Form 990 e-file XML — one row per filing (OBJECT_ID) for the IRS receipt year. The provider reads the per-year index CSV, then streams each TEOS XML zip, extracting header identity and Part I summary financials with version-defensive local-name matching across 990 / 990-EZ / 990-PF. NTEE is not in the XML — join to exempt_org_master on ein. Joins to ref/EIN. Source: apps.irs.gov/pub/epostcard/990/xml/{YEAR}/.
tables.name: exempt_org_990

tables.comment: Federal obligations summarized by awarding agency x fiscal year, from the USAspending Spending Explorer (type=agency, period=12 == full FY through Sep). Amounts are cumulative obligations. Joins semantically to fedregister.agencies by name. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/spending/.
tables.name: usaspending_by_agency

tables.comment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance state x fiscal year — the spatial counterpart to the SOI revenue tables and one level up from the county-grain usaspending_by_county. Carries obligated_amount (all award types) alongside obligated_amount_excl_loans, which drops award types '07'/'08' (loans): loans report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's, which inflates place-of-performance totals for states with large loan servicers. CMS-funded awards are likewise attributed to the Medicare Administrative Contractor's state (North Dakota, Minnesota and Indiana host contractors paying Medicare claims for beneficiaries nationwide), so obligated_amount and obligated_amount_excl_loans are not a measure of spending landing in the state and must not be divided by population to rank states; use obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin for that. For per-capita, join census.acs_population rather than a stored figure here. From USAspending spending_by_geography (geo_layer=state, all award types, FY expressed as Oct-Sep). Joins to geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.
tables.name: usaspending_by_state

tables.comment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance county x fiscal year — the county-grain counterpart to usaspending_by_state and the outlay side of soi_income_by_county. From USAspending spending_by_geography (geo_layer=county, all award types, FY expressed as Oct-Sep); ~2,800 counties per year. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Award types span contracts, IDVs, grants, direct payments and loans, so totals are wider than a contracts-only USAspending screen — filter in SQL if you need the A/B/C/D contract slice alone. Carries obligated_amount_excl_loans alongside obligated_amount because loans (award types '07'/'08') report face value at the lender/servicer's place of performance rather than the borrower's. For per-capita, join census.acs_population rather than using USAspending's own population reference, which is 2020 decennial. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.
tables.name: usaspending_by_county

tables.comment: Federal spending summarized by place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the district-grain counterpart to usaspending_by_state and usaspending_by_county. From USAspending spending_by_geography (geo_layer=district, all award types, FY expressed as Oct-Sep); one call per fiscal year returns all 442 districts in a single unpaginated response (435 numbered districts, at-large single-district states as district "00", and non-voting delegate districts for DC/PR/GU/VI/AS/MP as district "98"). Carries obligated_amount (all award types) alongside obligated_amount_excl_loans and obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin for the same reasons as usaspending_by_state/usaspending_by_county — see those tables' comments for the nationwide evidence. obligated_amount_contracts isolates procurement contract/IDV awards specifically (D-278), since obligated_amount alone mixes contracts with grants, loans, and direct payments indistinguishably. cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly (state FIPS + district number), no crosswalk needed. Does NOT carry a recipient/contractor-name dimension — USAspending's award-level search (spending_by_award, already used by UsaSpendingAwardSearchProvider for the broadband_*_awards tables) is paginated per-award rather than pre-aggregated, so a full recipient-concentration table across all 442 districts is a materially heavier build, deliberately left as a separate follow-up rather than folded into this one. For per-capita, join census.acs_population rather than a stored figure here. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.
tables.name: usaspending_by_district

tables.comment: Top 100 recipients by obligated dollar amount for each place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the recipient/contractor-name counterpart to usaspending_by_district, deferred from that table's build as "materially heavier" until a cheaper mechanism was confirmed live: USAspending's spending_by_category/recipient endpoint accepts a place_of_performance_locations filter shaped {country, state, district_current} and returns a server-side pre-aggregated, pre-ranked (descending by amount) recipient list in a single unpaginated call per district/year -- no per-award pagination needed, unlike UsaSpendingAwardSearchProvider's mechanism for the broadband_*_awards tables. SCOPE: exactly the top 100 recipients per district per year, matching the API's own page-size ceiling (limit=100 is the max; 500 is rejected as "above max '100'") -- not an attempt at every recipient in a district. A district with concentrated spending is fully captured; one with many small, dispersed recipients below the 100th rank is not. An aggregate "MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS" row (null recipient_id/uei/duns) appears in most districts for sub-reporting- threshold transactions USAspending itself buckets together, and is kept as a real ranked row. recipient_duns is the endpoint's "code" field (9-digit legacy DUNS-shaped identifier); recipient_uei is USAspending's own UEI when known; recipient_id is USAspending's internal recipient hash (present even when DUNS/UEI are not, except for the MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS aggregate). cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly, decoded the same way as usaspending_by_district. YEAR SCOPE: defaults to the 2 most recent complete fiscal years (usaspending_recipient_district_year_range), narrower than usaspending_by_district's 2018-present default -- this table makes one API call per (year, district) versus that table's 3 calls per year total, so a full 2018-present backfill is ~442x heavier; GOVDATA_START_YEAR overrides for a wider backfill when wanted. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/ (plus one spending_by_geography call per year to enumerate current districts, matching usaspending_by_district's own district list rather than a hard-coded one).
tables.name: usaspending_recipients_by_district

tables.comment: Top 100 procurement-contract recipients by obligated dollar amount for each place-of-performance congressional district x fiscal year — the contracts-only counterpart to usaspending_recipients_by_district. The ranking is computed server-side by USAspending's spending_by_category/recipient endpoint over contract and IDV award types only (award_type_codes A, B, C, D, IDV_A-IDV_E; the same set as usaspending_by_district.obligated_amount_contracts), so grant, direct-payment and loan recipients never occupy a rank. Use this table, not usaspending_recipients_by_district, for "which contractors dominate a district" questions; the all-award-types table ranks universities, health systems and benefit administrators alongside contractors. Same columns, same request shape and same top-100 ceiling (the API's page-size maximum) as usaspending_recipients_by_district: a district with concentrated contract spending is fully captured, one with many small dispersed contractors below the 100th rank is not. An aggregate "MULTIPLE RECIPIENTS" row (null recipient_id/uei/duns) is USAspending's own bucket for sub-reporting-threshold transactions; it is kept as a ranked row and flagged by is_aggregate_recipient. recipient_duns is the endpoint's "code" field (9-digit legacy DUNS-shaped identifier); recipient_uei is USAspending's own UEI when known; recipient_id is USAspending's internal recipient hash. cd_fips matches geo.congressional_districts.cd_fips exactly. A district's obligated_amount here is not bounded by usaspending_by_district.obligated_amount_contracts for that district/year: the district total nets every recipient's transactions, including large downward de-obligations from recipients outside this table's top 100, while each row here is one recipient's own gross positive sum. YEAR SCOPE: defaults to the 2 most recent complete fiscal years (usaspending_recipient_district_year_range); one API call per (year, district), so GOVDATA_START_YEAR widens it at ~8 minutes per added year. Joins to geo.congressional_districts via cd_fips. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_category/recipient/ (plus one spending_by_geography call per year to enumerate current districts).
tables.name: usaspending_contract_recipients_by_district

tables.comment: Social Security and Medicare spending by place-of-performance state x fiscal year, isolated by CFDA/assistance-listing number rather than derived from usaspending_by_state's award-type totals — the entitlement-program counterpart to that table and to ssa_benefits_by_geography (which carries SSA's own county-grain administrative beneficiary/program detail but lags further due to its Wayback-archive dependency). One row per state x program x fiscal year: social_security_retirement (CFDA 96.002, SSA Old-Age and Survivors Insurance), medicare_hospital_insurance (CFDA 93.773, Medicare Part A), medicare_supplementary_medical_insurance (CFDA 93.774, Medicare Part B) — one POST per program per fiscal year against filters.program_numbers, same endpoint and geo_layer=state scope as usaspending_by_state. Social Security's per-state totals reflect the beneficiary's actual state. The two Medicare programs inherit the same place-of-performance distortion documented on usaspending_by_state's obligated_amount_excl_loans_excl_cms_admin column: CMS-funded awards report place of performance at the Medicare Administrative Contractor's location, not the beneficiary's, so states hosting a MAC (e.g. ND/Noridian, MN, IN, KY, PA, SC, CT) show implausibly large totals relative to population — confirmed live at FY2025 scale for both Medicare programs here. Not an import defect; use ssa_benefits_by_geography or a per-capita/population -normalized read for a beneficiary-state view of Medicare spending. Joins to geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/.
tables.name: entitlement_spending_by_state

tables.comment: Small Business Administration 7(a) and 504 loan approvals (FOIA public data), one row per approved loan — federal credit activity by borrower geography, industry, lender, and approval fiscal year. Fanned out by program; each program is split across several year-range CSVs on the source site (year is a data column, not a partition), all streamed and concatenated by SbaLoansProvider. Reissued quarterly, so the whole program partition is overwritten each run. Joins to geo.state_ref via borrower_state. Source: data.sba.gov 7(a)-504 FOIA. borrower_name and lender_name are unstructured — this table carries no EIN column, so there is no exact hub-key join. ref.canonical_org_entity carries each as an already-resolved identity (sba_borrower_name, sba_lender_name, each with an LEI when matched); join there on the name rather than re-running a fuzzy match against gleif_entities.legal_name by hand.
tables.name: sba_loan_approvals

tables.comment: USDA ReConnect (CFDA 10.752) award-level broadband infrastructure grants and loan-grant combinations — one row per award, with recipient, dollar amount, performance period, and recipient location (county-grain via county_fips). A full crawl each run (not year-partitioned): the award-search endpoint has no reliable date-filter parameter that matches how award records are dated (obligation vs. performance-start vary by award), and the whole result set is small enough (low hundreds of awards) that a full refresh is cheap. Closes the ReConnect third of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap — BEAD is the sibling broadband_bead_state_allocations table (state-grain only); RDOF/CAF-II are FCC/USAC-administered, not CFDA awards, so they aren't reachable through this endpoint at all (CAF-II location data is instead sourced from USAC's own open-data platform, see broadband_caf_deployment_locations). Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05 — grants only, no contracts/loans in this program).
tables.name: broadband_reconnect_awards

tables.comment: ARRA (American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, 2009) broadband stimulus award-level grants — one row per award, with recipient, dollar amount, performance period, and recipient location (county-grain via county_fips). Covers both ARRA broadband programs: NTIA's Broadband Technology Opportunities Program (BTOP, CFDA 11.557, middle-mile/institutional/public-computing infrastructure) and RUS's Broadband Initiatives Program (BIP, CFDA 10.855, last-mile rural infrastructure). DQ-validated 2026-09-11: real awards under both programs (e.g. BTOP's EAGLE-NET ALLIANCE, $100.6M, Broomfield County CO; BIP awards to rural school districts and health clinics). Closes the ARRA third of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap alongside broadband_reconnect_awards (ReConnect) and broadband_bead_state_allocations (BEAD, state-grain only); RDOF/CAF-II remain FCC/USAC-administered, not CFDA awards — see broadband_high_cost_disbursements (carrier/state grain — RDOF has no address-level source publicly available) and broadband_caf_deployment_locations. A one-time, closed-out 2009-2011 program: full crawl each run (not year-partitioned), whole result set small enough (low thousands of awards across both CFDA numbers, DQ-confirmed: 241 for 11.557 + 2,454 for 10.855) that a full refresh is cheap. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05 — grants only, no contracts/loans in either program).
tables.name: broadband_arra_awards

tables.comment: FHWA bridge-specific award-level grants from USAspending — one row per award, with recipient, dollar amount, performance period, and recipient location (county-grain via county_fips; state_abbr supports GROUP BY state totals). Covers the IIJA Bridge Formula Program (CFDA 20.263, formula funds apportioned to every state DOT for bridge replacement/rehabilitation) and the discretionary Bridge Investment Program (CFDA 20.264, competitive large -bridge awards). DQ-validated 2026-09-14: real large bridge projects (e.g. CFDA 20.263's Vincent Thomas Bridge deck replacement in Los Angeles County CA, $152.6M; CFDA 20.264's Brent Spence Bridge Corridor OH/KY, $400M). recipient_name/state_abbr/county_fips are the state DOT's registered address, not necessarily the bridge's physical location — the same convention as this table's sibling USAspending award tables (broadband_reconnect_awards, broadband_arra_awards); the award description usually names the specific bridge/corridor. Closes the program-level counterpart to usaspending_by_state (which carries only an undifferentiated per-state total with no program breakdown): filtering this table to cfda_number = '20.263' isolates Bridge Formula Program dollars per state, the gap this table was built for. A full crawl each run (not year-partitioned): the award-search endpoint has no reliable date-filter parameter that matches how award records are dated (obligation vs. performance-start vary by award), and the result set is small enough (low thousands of awards across both CFDA numbers, DQ-confirmed: 3,380 for 20.263 + 33 for 20.264) that a full refresh is cheap. The Competitive Highway Bridge Program (CFDA 20.267) and Competitive Type 3 Highway Bridge Program (20.198) exist in the CFDA catalog but had zero awarded grants as of 2026-09-14 — not included here; add them if/when they start awarding. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05 — grants only, no contracts/loans in either program).
tables.name: usaspending_bridge_awards

tables.comment: NTIA Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment program (CFDA 11.035) prime grant awards — one row per state/territory broadband office, since BEAD's federal award record is state-grain only: each state gets one lump-sum grant which it then sub-awards to individual ISPs by county/project area, and those sub-awards are not themselves federal-award records reachable from this endpoint (confirmed live: this table has on the order of 56 rows, one per state/territory/DC, not the thousands a county-level table would have). Useful for state-level BEAD allocation totals; does NOT close the county-grain half of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap — see broadband_reconnect_awards and broadband_caf_deployment_locations for the two programs with real sub-state grain. Source: api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/ (program_numbers filter, award types 02/03/04/05).
tables.name: broadband_bead_state_allocations

tables.comment: FCC Connect America Fund Phase II (CAF-II) subsidized broadband buildout — one row per deployed location (near-address grain: lat/long, street address, and 15-digit census_block, whose first 5 digits are the county FIPS), filed annually by the carrier as it completes buildout milestones. Sourced from USAC's own open-data platform (opendata.usac.org, dataset r59r-rpip — the same underlying "CAF Map" data usaspending itself can't reach, since CAF-II is an FCC/USAC Universal Service Fund disbursement, not a CFDA federal-assistance award), filtered to fund_type IN ('CAF II', 'CAF II Auc') — this dataset also carries ACAM/ACAM II/CAF-BLS/RBE/AK Plan rows for other high-cost programs, out of scope here. RDOF rows do not yet appear in this feed (RDOF winners are still mid-buildout under a 10-year plan; only carrier-level disbursement/location-count totals exist for RDOF today, not individual addresses) — closes the CAF-II third of the "federal broadband award geography" sourcing gap, not RDOF. ~4.8M rows across 2015-2025 (2016-2021 the heaviest reporting years). Joins to geo.counties by taking the first 5 digits of census_block.
tables.name: broadband_caf_deployment_locations

tables.comment: Federal Universal Service Fund high-cost-program disbursements at Eligible Telecommunication Carrier (ETC) x month grain, from USAC's own open-data platform (opendata.usac.org, dataset w6qn-gx72). Covers every current-generation high-cost program's dollar flows to individual carriers by month: RDOF, CAF-II (annual + Auction 903), ACAM/ACAM-II, CAF-BLS (Broadband Loop Support), the Alaska Plan, RBE (Rural Broadband Experiments), and legacy programs (HCL, HCM, ICLS, IAS, Mobility I, LSS, SNA) still paying out on prior obligations. Together with fiscal.broadband_caf_deployment_locations (CAF-II served addresses), fiscal.broadband_reconnect_awards (USDA ReConnect), and fiscal.broadband_bead_state_allocations (NTIA BEAD) this is the fourth broadband-program table — carrier/state grain, not the county/tract grain the "federal broadband award geography" gap originally asked for (RDOF has no address-level source publicly available today; winners are still mid-buildout under a 10-year plan). Joins to sibling broadband tables by study_area_code. Source: opendata.usac.org/resource/w6qn-gx72.json.
tables.name: broadband_high_cost_disbursements

tables.comment: SSA OASDI and SSI beneficiary counts and total benefit dollars by county x program x benefit type x year — the largest federal mandatory-spending stream, geo-keyed and comparable per county against soi_income_by_county and usaspending_by_state. SSA publishes only multi-sheet XLSX reports on a WAF-protected host that 403s non-browser clients, so the provider fetches the Wayback-archived workbook (oasdi_sc / ssi_sc) and parses the per-state county tables (Table 4 counts + Table 5 dollars for OASDI; Table 3 for SSI). The ANSI Code column carries the county FIPS directly. beneficiary_type is a mutually-exclusive published category (OASDI leaves sum to 'total'). Amounts are the December total monthly benefits, in whole USD; avg_monthly is per beneficiary. SSI per-category dollars are not published (only the total).
tables.name: ssa_benefits_by_geography

tables.comment: County-level Social Security and SSI recipiency and dollars DERIVED from the Census ACS 5-year estimates — a fully open-API, WAF-free complement to the Wayback-sourced ssa_benefits_by_geography (which alone carries the SSA administrative beneficiary-type/program detail). One row per county x ACS vintage. These are SURVEY ESTIMATES on a HOUSEHOLD basis (not SSA administrative person counts): they cannot split OASI vs DI or beneficiary type, but give the geographic distribution of Social Security / SSI receipt and aggregate dollars with no archive.org dependency. Aggregate-dollar figures are survey-reported and run below SSA administrative totals. Source: api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/acs5 (B19055/B19056/B19065/B19066).
tables.name: ssa_benefits_by_geography_acs

tables.comment: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) persons/households participating and total/average monthly benefits, by state x year x month — the nutrition- assistance counterpart to ssa_benefits_by_geography's income-benefits data, both geo-keyed and comparable against usaspending_by_state. USDA FNA publishes one zip covering FY1989-present (one workbook per fiscal year inside), not a per-year URL, so this table has no year fetch dimension — the provider parses the full history from one download and materialize partitions by the year column found in each row, same as fiscal's other single-workbook bulk sources. Excludes P-EBT (Pandemic EBT) figures, which USDA reports separately. FY2019 (Oct 2018-Sep 2019) carries a source-published distortion: because of the partial federal government shutdown, most February 2019 benefits were issued in January 2019, so month 1 of FY2019 shows roughly double a normal month's total_benefits_usd and month 2 shows almost none, and the per-state fiscal-year Total row (month IS NULL) averages persons and households over those two months as published, which pulls the FY2019 average persons_participating below the surrounding months.
tables.name: snap_benefits_by_geography

tables.comment: OMB-approved apportionments (SF-132 schedules) for every federal budget account, one row per schedule line of each approval iteration, by fiscal year FY2022-present. Apportionment is the step where OMB releases appropriated budget authority to an agency by quarter or by project, so this is where withheld, deferred or footnoted-away funds show up: the free-text footnote_text column carries OMB's conditions on the money, including language withholding funds pending review and proposed-rescission or deferral notices. It is the account-level counterpart to mts_outlays_by_function and federal_outlays_by_function, which stop at function totals.
