tables.comment: HUD "A Picture of Subsidized Households" — the all-HUD-programs summary of assisted-housing units and residents, by census tract (December 2020 snapshot): total_units, people_total, people_per_unit, avg_hh_income, and pct_disabled. One row per tract (program = 'Summary of All HUD Programs' only). Static table: the whole layer is re-paginated and the partition overwritten each run. For the richer county-level, per-program, per-year profile (occupancy, tenant rent, HUD spending, more demographic shares) see hud_subsidized_county. census_tract is the 11-digit tract GEOID; joins to geo.counties via county_fips and to geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Source: HUD Open Data ArcGIS Snapshot_HUD_Picture_Subsidized_Households FeatureServer.
tables.name: hud_subsidized_housing

tables.comment: HUD "A Picture of Subsidized Households" at county × HUD-program grain, from the annual county workbook (COUNTY_<year>_2020census.xlsx). One row per (county, program) — 'Summary of All HUD Programs', 'Public Housing', 'Housing Choice Vouchers', 'Project-Based Section 8', etc. — with the full resident profile the ArcGIS tract snapshot (hud_subsidized_housing) omits: occupancy, average income, tenant rent, HUD spending, and percent minority / female-headed / elderly / disabled. HUD's -1 / 'NA' suppression sentinels are nulled. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips. Source: huduser.gov/portal/datasets/pictures/files.
tables.name: hud_subsidized_county

tables.comment: NYC Department of Homeless Services (DHS) Daily Report — the daily number of individuals and families residing in the DHS shelter system, citywide (no borough/facility breakdown; sourced elsewhere on NYC Open Data as a separate dataset, a documented follow-up). One row per calendar date. NYC Open Data splits this series across two Socrata resources: k46n-sa2m ("current", 2021-03-01 onward) and dwrg-kzni ("historical", 2013-08-21 through 2021-02-28) — a clean, non-overlapping boundary confirmed live, despite each resource's own metadata description claiming a start/end date that would read as an ~8-week overlap (see NycDhsShelterCensusTransformer). families_with_children_in_shelter / adult_families_in_shelter rows count distinct family units, not individuals; total_individuals_in_shelter is the citywide census total. No FK — this is a citywide daily aggregate with no state/county grain. Source: data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/DHS-Daily-Report/k46n-sa2m (current) and /dwrg-kzni (historical).
tables.name: homeless_shelter_census

tables.comment: HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) homeless counts by Continuum of Care (CoC), one row per (year, coc_number, metric_name). Source workbook is wide (HUD adds subpopulation/ demographic breakout columns most years - 25 columns in 2007 growing to 1,300+ by 2024) so this is melted long-format rather than carrying 1,300+ typed columns; metric_name is the source column header verbatim (e.g. 'Sheltered ES Homeless - Age 18 to 24', 'Overall Homeless Veterans') - see the HUD workbook's own 'field list, all years' sheet for the full taxonomy. A blank/suppressed source cell is omitted rather than written as a null count row. Includes a national total row (coc_number = 'TOTAL', coc_name = 'Total', state_abbr null - HUD leaves CoC Number blank for this row in the source). MO-604 spans Missouri and Kansas and is reported here as one combined CoC row; the companion by-state file splits its counts between MO and KS, so per-state rollups from this table will not exactly match hud_pit_counts_by_state for those two states. Source: huduser.gov/portal/sites/ default/files/xls/2007-2024-PIT-Counts-by-CoC.xlsb (annual PIT count cycle).
tables.name: hud_pit_counts_by_coc

tables.comment: HUD Point-in-Time (PIT) homeless counts by state/territory, one row per (year, state_abbr, metric_name). Companion file to hud_pit_counts_by_coc at state grain - same wide-to-long melt for the same reason (1,300+ source columns by 2024). Includes a national total row (state_abbr = 'Total'). A blank/suppressed source cell is omitted rather than written as a null count row. Source: huduser.gov/portal/sites/ default/files/xls/2007-2024-PIT-Counts-by-State.xlsb (annual PIT count cycle).
tables.name: hud_pit_counts_by_state

lands.comment: U.S. federal public lands data covering USDA Forest Service, National Park Service, and Bureau of Land Management units. Includes land management boundaries, timber sale program contracts, forest inventory estimates, NPS visitation statistics, and Office of Natural Resources Revenue (ONRR) mineral royalty payments. Enables analysis of extractive industry activity on federal land, tourism economics, and timber/paper company revenue risk via SEC filings.

tables.comment: USDA Forest Service National Forest and Grassland unit boundaries. ~175 units across 10 USFS regions. Reference/dimension table — FK target for timber_sales.forest_code via forest_id. Updated annually post-fire-season (October). geometry_wkt carries the unit's own WGS84 boundary polygon, sourced from the same ArcGIS query at ingest time (no separate spatial join needed to plot or intersect an individual forest); for federal-fee ownership share by county across all agencies, use lands.padus_federal_fee_lands / lands.county_federal_fee_land_share instead, since PAD-US's own_type/mang_name lets that dataset be filtered or compared across USFS, BLM, and NPS in one place.
tables.name: national_forests

tables.comment: USDA Forest Service timber harvest activities from FACTS EDW. One row per completed harvest activity. Joins to national_forests via forest_code and to geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Units_accomplished and uom describe harvest volume (CCF, MBF, ACRE, etc.). Enables analysis of federal timber activity by forest, district, and year. Also carries cost_per_uom (USD per unit of measure) for harvest cost analysis. Source: EDW_TimberHarvest_01/MapServer/{layer} where layer is dispatched per year by UsfsTimberLayerResolver — layer 11 covers 2021+, layer 0 covers 2011-2020, and layers 1-7 could in principle reach as far back as 1820, but this table is only ever fetched from GOVDATA_START_YEAR forward (see observedCoverage below for the real floor actually loaded) — the 1820 figure describes what the source's older layers contain, not what's in this table. The service hard-caps maxRecordCount at 2000 regardless of the requested resultRecordCount (a single year can hold 4x that); UsfsFactsTransformer pages on exceededTransferLimit via resultOffset rather than making one request per year. All layers publish the identical 71-field schema.
tables.name: timber_sales

tables.comment: USDA Forest Service Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) state-level estimates derived from per-state {ST}_COND.csv files inside the FIA datamart's per-state ZIP archives (apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/{state}_CSV.zip). One row per inventory_year × state × forest_type_group × ownership_class. Filtered to COND_STATUS_CD=1 (accessible forest land). Basal area is a CONDPROP_UNADJ-weighted average of BALIVE. Joins to geo.state_ref via state_fips. ETL fans out across states; cached per-state archives in $GOVDATA_CACHE_DIR/lands/ are shared across workers. Materialization keeps state as a row column, not a partition column, so that Iceberg per-partition compaction merges the 55 per-state ETL flushes into a single nationwide parquet.
tables.name: forest_inventory

tables.comment: USDA FIA tree-level metrics derived from per-state {ST}_TREE.csv joined to {ST}_COND.csv (both inside the per-state ZIP archive at apps.fs.usda.gov/fia/datamart/CSV/{state}_CSV.zip). One row per inventory_year × state × forest_type_group × ownership_class. Columns are CONDPROP_UNADJ-weighted averages across live trees (STATUSCD=1) in accessible forest conditions (COND_STATUS_CD=1). Join to forest_inventory on (state_fips, inventory_year, forest_type_group, ownership_class) for combined basal-area + volume + carbon analysis. ETL fans out across states.
tables.name: forest_metrics

tables.comment: USDA FIA per-plot identification from per-state {ST}_PLOT.csv. One row per FIA plot. Lat/lon are USDA's publicly-released "fuzzed" coordinates (perturbed so exact plot locations cannot be inferred — FIADB P2 User Guide §2.5.1). plot_cn is the FIA-wide unique plot identifier; join targets are TREE/COND/ SEEDLING via PLT_CN. ETL fans out across states.
tables.name: fia_plots

tables.comment: USDA FIA growth-removal-mortality (GRM) annualized estimates by state, inventory year, species, and estimation type. Derived by joining per-state {ST}_TREE_GRM_ESTN.csv against {ST}_TREE.csv on TRE_CN to attach SPCD, then aggregating per-tree ANN_NET_GROWTH/REMOVALS/MORTALITY into per-group totals. Units are determined by ESTN_UNITS for the row's ESTN_TYPE (typically cubic feet for volume estimates and square feet for basal area). ETL fans out across states.
tables.name: fia_tree_grm

tables.comment: USDA FIA seedling regeneration estimates by state, inventory year, and species, derived from per-state {ST}_SEEDLING.csv. seedlings_per_acre is the sum of TPA_UNADJ across plot-conditions; seedling_count is the sum of microplot TREECOUNT observations. Pairs with forest_metrics for tree+regeneration analytics.
tables.name: fia_seedlings

tables.comment: USDA FIA down-woody-material biomass aggregated by state, inventory year, and debris category (coarse_woody, fine_woody, duff_litter). Derived from per-state {ST}_COND_DWM_CALC.csv. tons_per_acre is the condition-area weighted mean of the FIA per-condition adjusted dry-biomass tonnage for the category.
tables.name: fia_down_woody_debris

tables.comment: USDA FIA invasive plant species observations aggregated by state, inventory year, and species code, derived from per-state {ST}_INVASIVE_SUBPLOT_SPP.csv. cover_pct_avg is the mean COVER_PCT across reporting subplots. Not every state samples invasives every cycle.
tables.name: fia_invasives

tables.comment: FIA stratification stratum — carries EXPNS (the expansion factor, acres represented per plot) and the ADJ_FACTOR_* adjustments. Join fia_pop_plot_stratum_assgn to attach a plot to its stratum, then weight by EXPNS to turn plot observations into design-based population totals. Without this table only per-plot averages are possible, never state or regional estimates. Carried at its published grain (one row per source row) from per-state {ST}_POP_STRATUM.csv, because aggregating it would defeat its purpose.
tables.name: fia_pop_stratum

tables.comment: Assigns each plot (PLT_CN) to a stratum (STRATUM_CN) within an evaluation (EVALID). This is the join key between plot-level observations and the stratification that expands them to population totals. Carried at its published grain (one row per source row) from per-state {ST}_POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN.csv, because aggregating it would defeat its purpose.
tables.name: fia_pop_plot_stratum_assgn

tables.comment: Estimation unit — the geographic partition a stratification is built within, carrying its land and total area. The denominator for area-based estimates. Carried at its published grain (one row per source row) from per-state {ST}_POP_ESTN_UNIT.csv, because aggregating it would defeat its purpose.
tables.name: fia_pop_estn_unit

tables.comment: Evaluation group: the set of evaluations that together form one reportable inventory cycle for a state (EVAL_GRP, e.g. 'AK2023'). Carried at its published grain (one row per source row) from per-state {ST}_POP_EVAL_GRP.csv, because aggregating it would defeat its purpose.
tables.name: fia_pop_eval_grp

tables.comment: Maps an evaluation to the attributes it supports, so a consumer can tell which estimates a given EVALID is valid for. Carried at its published grain (one row per source row) from per- state {ST}_POP_EVAL_ATTRIBUTE.csv, because aggregating it would defeat its purpose.
tables.name: fia_pop_eval_attribute

tables.comment: USDA FIA population evaluations — the statistically-valid samples used to publish state estimates. Joins {ST}_POP_EVAL.csv with {ST}_POP_EVAL_TYP.csv on EVAL_CN to emit one row per (evaluation, evaluation type) pair. eval_type values include EXPVOL (volume), EXPCURR (current area), EXPGROW, EXPMORT, EXPREMV, etc.
tables.name: fia_pop_evaluations

tables.comment: National Park Service unit boundaries — parks, monuments, recreation areas, seashores, parkways, and all other NPS-designated units. ~430 units. Reference and dimension table; FK target for nps_visitation.unit_code. Joins to geo.state_ref and geo.counties for gateway-community economic impact analysis. Updated annually in April following annual report administrative updates. geometry_wkt carries the unit's own WGS84 boundary polygon, sourced from the same ArcGIS query at ingest time; this table still carries no county_fips column of its own (see nps_visitation's comment), so a county-grain join needs a spatial predicate against geometry_wkt (e.g. DuckDB ST_Intersects with geo.counties), following the pattern lands.county_federal_fee_land_share already uses for padus_federal_fee_lands.
tables.name: nps_units

tables.comment: National Park Service monthly visitation statistics from the IRMA Statistics API. One row per unit_code × visit_year × visit_month (no annual summary rows), with recreation_visits and non_recreation_visits as the two visit-count metrics. Joins to nps_units via unit_code. See lands_nps_gateway_impact and lands_nps_gateway_employment for pre-built annual aggregations per unit; note nps_units carries no county_fips, so county-level employment correlation is not directly supported.
tables.name: nps_visitation

tables.comment: Bureau of Land Management administrative unit boundaries — field offices and district offices that manage federal subsurface mineral rights, grazing allotments, and surface use permits. ~150 field offices. Primarily useful as a geographic reference for joining extractive industry activity to SEC filings and FEC oil/gas sector donor geography. Updated annually in June. geometry_wkt is the office's own point location only (this table's source layer carries point geometry, not the administrative boundary polygon — see the column comment); for a federal-fee land boundary/ownership polygon to spatially join against counties or fire perimeters, use lands.padus_federal_fee_lands instead.
tables.name: blm_field_offices

tables.comment: Office of Natural Resources Revenue (ONRR) royalty payments for oil, gas, coal, and other minerals extracted from federal and tribal lands, full history from FY 2004 in a single bulk download. Row grain is every descriptive column together (fiscal_year, land_class, land_category, state_name, county_name, county_fips, offshore_region, revenue_type, mineral_lease_type, commodity, product) — revenue is the only measure. county_fips alone does not identify a row: ONRR carries multiple distinct rows sharing one FIPS (e.g. "Kenai (Pre)" vs "Kenai (Post)" county_name), and offshore rows (null state_name/county_name/county_fips) are distinguished by offshore_region instead. Primary financial link between BLM-managed subsurface rights and SEC 10-K disclosures for E&P and mining companies. Source: revenuedata.onrr.gov (domain moved from revenuedata.doi.gov in 2024).
tables.name: onrr_revenues

tables.comment: Federal oil & gas lease acreage published by the Bureau of Land Management, one row per (state, fiscal_year), covering FY 2001-present. Two measures per row: leased_acres (BLM "Acreage in Effect", Table 2 — total federal oil & gas lease acreage still in force as of that fiscal year end) and producing_acres (BLM "Acreage of Producing Leases", Table 6 — the subset actually producing). Sourced from one combined XLSX per fiscal-year release; this table unpivots both wide sheets and joins on (state, fiscal_year) so each state-year gets a single row with both measures. Enables per-acre royalty-productivity analysis when joined to lands.onrr_revenues on (state, fiscal_year) — revenue divided by producing_acres gives royalty per producing acre, matching the exact question this table was sourced for. Coverage is **Federal-only, excludes Indian leases** per BLM's own note in the source workbook — this is the same scope as onrr_revenues' Federal/land_class rows and joins cleanly on that basis. Table is a static snapshot: the whole file is re-fetched each run and the partition overwritten; history lives in Iceberg snapshots. No key required. **URL drift caveat**: BLM publishes each new fiscal year's file at a URL that encodes the release month in the path (docs/2025-07/... for FY24 release, docs/2026-04/... for FY25 release, and so on). Rather than chase that per year, this table pins the URL to the FY24 file (published July 2025), whose combined XLSX already carries FY 2001-2024 in one download. On next FY release, update the URL to the newer file (whose combined XLSX will cover all years through the new one) — BLM's landing page at blm.gov/programs/energy-and-minerals/oil-and-gas/oil-and-gas-statistics is the authoritative index for locating the current URL. **Known source quirk**: producing_acres exceeds leased_acres in a small number of rows (10 of 1200 in the FY24 file — Illinois, New York, Pennsylvania, Tennessee; excess ranges from 0.25 to ~150 acres). All affected states are minor producers; no major federal-lease state (Wyoming, New Mexico, Colorado, etc.) exhibits this. This reflects a reporting-boundary/timing difference between BLM's Table 2 (Acreage in Effect, point-in-time snapshot) and Table 6 (Producing Acres) rather than a join or parsing defect — treated as an expected small discrepancy, not a data quality failure.
tables.name: blm_oil_gas_acreage

tables.comment: DOI Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) — federal payments to local governments for tax-exempt federal land within their boundaries, one row per (fiscal_year, state_code, area_name). Counterpart to onrr_revenues (federal mineral-revenue sharing): PILT compensates for the property-tax base federal land removes, independent of resource extraction. area_type is derived from the source label's own COUNTY/PARISH/BOROUGH/TOWN/... wording (null when the label carries none, e.g. DC/Guam/the Virgin Islands, each a single territory-wide row) rather than assumed from the state, since some states mix area types (Vermont's table has both towns and county-level subtotal rows). No bulk export exists; one fetch per (fiscal_yr, state_code) returns that state's full county list. Source: pilt.doi.gov/counties.cfm.
tables.name: pilt_county_payments

tables.comment: Veterans Health Administration facility roster — VA medical centers (VAMC), community-based outpatient clinics (CBOC), Vet Centers (VCTR), VA nursing homes (VANH), and residential rehabilitation treatment programs (RRTP), geocoded. One row per facility (1,046 confirmed live). Answers "nearest VA facility to a given location" directly via latitude/longitude — the corpus previously had no way to do this, only a rurality proxy via census.acs_veterans joined to health.ahrf_physician_supply's RUCC. Joins to geo.counties via county_fips and geo.state_ref via state_abbr. Source: HIFLD Veterans Health Administration Medical Facilities ArcGIS FeatureServer.
tables.name: va_facilities

tables.comment: USGS GAP Analysis Project's authoritative federal-fee-land layer (Federal_Fee_Managers_Authoritative_PADUS, part of PAD-US) — one row per federal-fee-land polygon (~5,361 features) with owning/managing agency (own_type/own_name, mang_type/mang_name), designation_type, state_abbr, acres, and a simplified WGS84 boundary polygon (geometry_wkt). Federal-fee ownership only (not the full multi-hundred-thousand-polygon PAD-US inventory across all ownership classes — state/tribal/local/NGO/private land is out of scope here). No county_fips column; assigning per-county ownership shares requires a spatial join (DuckDB ST_Intersects) against geo.counties, which is a natural follow-up view, not done at ingest time. Snapshot table with no year partition (refreshed via overwritePartitions). Answers the per-county, cross-agency federal-fee-ownership-share need behind D-054 in one place — own_type/mang_name lets a query filter or compare ownership across USFS, BLM, NPS, and other federal managers without joining three separately-sourced tables. national_forests and nps_units now also carry their own geometry_wkt (their unit's own boundary polygon, captured directly at ingest); blm_field_offices carries only a point location (see its column comment). Also gives disasters.wildfire_perimeters a federal-fee-land layer to compute federal-vs-nonfederal wildfire exposure against (D-176). Source: Federal_Fee_Managers_Authoritative_PADUS/FeatureServer/0 (official USGS GAP Analysis Project ArcGIS org, item v01gqwM5QqNysAAi). WARNING: do not SUM(acres) for a total federal-fee acreage figure — this layer's own rows are not mutually exclusive despite its "Authoritative" name. Verified live 2026-09-12 directly against the source FeatureServer (not an artifact of this table's ingestion — our own SUM(acres) matches the source's own aggregate query exactly): summing all 5,361 rows gives ~2.25B acres, near the entire land area of the US; even filtering to category='Fee' (ownership, excluding Proclamation boundaries) still gives ~2.10B acres. Grouping by mang_name shows BLM/USFS/NPS/USACE/USBR sums are each close to their independently known real totals (e.g. USFS ~193M acres, matching the National Forest System almost exactly) — the inflation is concentrated in FWS, whose rows include near-duplicate polygon pairs for the same unit at nearly identical (not exactly equal) acreage, e.g. Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument appears twice (310,260,466 and 310,260,380 acres), Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument three times (283,392,764 / 283,392,311 / 88,143,702 for a "Monument Original" sub-record), Mariana Trench NWR twice (50,559,347 / 50,559,316), Arctic NWR twice (19,637,182 / 19,637,012). This is a source data-quality defect in PAD-US's own authoritative layer, not fixable by de-duplicating on any single column here. A query needing a real distinct-area total should use CRS's published federal land figure (~640-650M acres) rather than SUM(acres) on this table, or compute a true union area via ST_Union/ST_Area over geometry_wkt (costly but correct). This table remains the right source for per-parcel attribute lookups, agency/designation filters, and spatial joins (e.g. against geo.counties or disasters.wildfire_perimeters) where exact row-for-row overlap doesn't matter.
tables.name: padus_federal_fee_lands

law.comment: The legal corpus, one source per group of tables. It currently holds the United States Code (codified general and permanent federal statutes) from the Office of the Law Revision Counsel's USLM XML release points at uscode.house.gov, one row per section (about 60,500 at release point 119-111), covering Titles 1-52 and 54 and the appendices to Titles 5 and 18. This is the current in-force text at the latest release point (release_point column, e.g. 119-111 = current through Public Law 119-111), replaced wholesale on each run — it is not a history of prior versions. is_positive_law separates titles Congress has enacted as law itself (e.g. Titles 5, 18, 28) from titles that are only prima facie evidence of the law (e.g. Titles 26 and 42). Regulations (CFR) and private or temporary laws are not in this schema; the Federal Register lives in the fedregister schema. Tables: usc_sections (section_text holds the operative text of each whole section for reading; source_credit holds the enactment history citing each Public Law and Statutes at Large page); usc_subsections (the same text cut at subsection, paragraph and clause boundaries into units of at most 2,000 characters, the field embedded for semantic search); and `bills` with its child tables, covering every bill and resolution introduced in Congress from the GovInfo Bill Status bulk data — status and sponsor in `bills`; action history, cosponsors, committee referrals and their activity, subject terms, published text, related bills, amendments and their actions and cosponsors, roll-call votes, titles, CRS summaries, CBO estimates, committee reports and editorial notes in `bill_actions`, `bill_cosponsors`, `bill_committees`, `bill_committee_activities`, `bill_subjects`, `bill_text_versions`, `bill_related_bills`, `bill_amendments`, `bill_amendment_actions`, `bill_amendment_cosponsors`, `bill_action_committees`, `bill_recorded_votes`, `bill_titles`, `bill_summaries`, `bill_cbo_cost_estimates`, `bill_committee_reports` and `bill_notes`; and federal lobbying disclosures from LDA.gov — `lobbying_filings` (LD-1 registrations and LD-2 quarterly reports: who lobbied for whom and for how much) with `lobbying_activities` (the issues, in free text that names bills), `lobbying_activity_lobbyists`, `lobbying_activity_government_entities`, `lobbying_foreign_entities`, `lobbying_affiliated_organizations` and `lobbying_conviction_disclosures`; LD-203 political-contribution reports in `lobbying_contribution_reports`, `lobbying_contribution_items` and `lobbying_contribution_pacs`; the registries `lobbyists`, `lobbying_registrants` and `lobbying_clients`; and the code lists `lobbying_issue_codes`, `lobbying_government_entity_codes`, `lobbying_filing_types` and `lobbying_contribution_item_types`. The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the lobbying data or analyses derived from it after retrieval from LDA.gov.

tables.comment: One row per section of the U.S. Code at the current OLRC release point. The operative text of the section is in section_text (statutory notes, tables of contents and editorial footnotes are excluded); the Public Law and Statutes at Large citations that enacted and amended it are in source_credit. Sections that were repealed, omitted or transferred keep their row (status says which) but have a null section_text because no operative text remains. Filter on is_positive_law for titles enacted as law, and on title_number/chapter_number for a subject area (e.g. title 26 = Internal Revenue Code, 42 = Public Health and Welfare, 15 = Commerce and Trade).
tables.name: usc_sections

tables.comment: One row per unit of a U.S. Code section: the section's operative text cut at its own subsection, paragraph and clause boundaries into pieces of at most 2,000 characters, in document order. Join to usc_sections on (title_number, section_number, section_seq) for the section's heading, hierarchy, status and enactment history. Sections with no operative text (repealed, omitted, transferred, or pointer-only) have no rows here. unit_path says which divisions a row covers, so a hit can be cited to the subsection, for example 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(1) to (a)(2).
tables.name: usc_subsections

tables.comment: Every bill and resolution introduced in the U.S. Congress, one row per bill, from the GovInfo Bill Status bulk data (the same data the Congress.gov API serves). Partitioned by `congress` (e.g. 119 = 2025-2026) and `bill_type`: hr (House bill), s (Senate bill), hjres / sjres (joint resolutions), hconres / sconres (concurrent resolutions), hres / sres (simple resolutions). `bill_number` is unique only within (congress, bill_type). `latest_action_text` / `latest_action_date` are the best single status signal (e.g. "Became Public Law No: 119-21.", "Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary."); `law_type` and `law_number` are populated only once a bill is enacted. Sponsor columns carry the first listed sponsor. `action_count` and `cosponsor_count` count the rows in bill_actions and bill_cosponsors for the same bill; committee referrals, subjects, text, related bills, amendments, votes, titles, summaries, CBO estimates, committee reports and notes are in the other bill_* tables (bill_committees, bill_subjects, bill_text_versions, bill_related_bills, bill_amendments, bill_recorded_votes, bill_titles, bill_summaries, bill_cbo_cost_estimates, bill_committee_reports, bill_notes, ...). The current Congress changes daily at the source and is re-pulled monthly; completed Congresses are static. The source publishes the 108th Congress onward; the default GOVDATA_START_YEAR (2010) starts at the 111th.
tables.name: bills

tables.comment: Every recorded action on every bill in `bills`, one row per action, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML — introduction, committee referral, markup, floor votes, passage, presentment, signing. Join to `bills` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number). `action_seq` numbers actions oldest-first starting at 1, so it stays fixed when later actions are added. `action_type` is the source's coarse category (observed in the 119th: IntroReferral, Committee, Floor, Calendars, Discharge, ResolvingDifferences, President, Veto, BecameLaw, NotUsed) and `action_code` its code (e.g. E40000). Only about a fifth of actions carry an `action_time`.
tables.name: bill_actions

tables.comment: Cosponsors of every bill in `bills`, one row per (bill, cosponsor), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. Join to `bills` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number) and to officials.members on `bioguide_id`. `is_original_cosponsor` is true for members who signed on at introduction; `withdrawn_date` is set when a cosponsor later withdrew. Bills with no cosponsors have no rows here. A member who withdrew and later re-signed appears twice, with different `sponsorship_date`; a few identical repeats also exist upstream (2 in the 108th-119th).
tables.name: bill_cosponsors

tables.comment: Committees and subcommittees a bill was referred to, one row per committee or subcommittee, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. Join to `bills` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number). `committee_system_code` is the Congress.gov committee code (e.g. hsju00 = House Judiciary). A subcommittee row (e.g. hsvr10) has `parent_committee_system_code` set to its full committee's code and NULL `chamber` and `committee_type`, which the source records only on the full committee. `committee_type` is Standing, Select, Special or Other. What each committee did with the bill (referred, markup, reported, hearings) is in bill_committee_activities.
tables.name: bill_committees

tables.comment: Every recorded committee activity on a bill, one row per (committee or subcommittee, activity), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. Join to bill_committees on (congress, bill_type, bill_number, committee_system_code). `activity_name` values include Referred To, Markup By, Reported By, Hearings By (full committee), Discharged From, Reported Original Measure and Bills of Interest - Exchange of Letters, spelled as the source publishes them — capitalization is not consistent (Referred To / Referred to). `activity_date` is a UTC timestamp. The source occasionally repeats an identical activity, so the rows have no unique key.
tables.name: bill_committee_activities

tables.comment: Congressional Research Service legislative subject terms assigned to a bill, one row per (bill, subject), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML — e.g. "Abortion", "Accounting and auditing". A bill can carry hundreds (H.R. 1 in the 119th has 239). The single broader policy area is `bills.policy_area`, not repeated here. Subjects are assigned some time after introduction, so a new bill may have none yet.
tables.name: bill_subjects

tables.comment: Every published text version of a bill, one row per (version, format), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML; the `url` points at the text on govinfo.gov. `version_type` follows the bill through Congress using GPO's stage names — Introduced in House/Senate, Referred in Senate, Reported in House, Reported to Senate, Placed on Calendar Senate, Engrossed in House/Senate, Engrossed Amendment House/Senate, Considered and Passed House/Senate, Agreed to House/Senate, Enrolled Bill, Public Law, and older stage names such as Additional Sponsors House and Committee Discharged Senate. `format_type` is set only for the "United States Legislative Markup" (USLM) file; the plain XML row has NULL `format_type`. A version whose text is not yet published has one row with NULL `url`, and some versions (e.g. Enrolled Bill) have NULL `version_date`. The source occasionally lists an identical version twice.
tables.name: bill_text_versions

tables.comment: Bills the Congressional Research Service, the House or GPO link to a bill, one row per (bill, related bill, relationship), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `relationship_type` is one of Related bill, Identical bill, Companion bill, Cross-Congress related bill, Contained in public law, Public law contains the text, Procedurally related (also spelled Procedurally-related in older files), Related document, Text similarities, PrimaryCompanionBillBecameLaw, SecondaryCompanionBillBecameLaw; `identified_by` says who made the link (CRS, House, Senate, U.S. Government Publishing Office). `related_bill_type` uses the same lowercase slugs as `bill_type` (hr, s, hres, ...), so (related_congress, related_bill_type, related_bill_number) joins straight back to `bills`. The `related_latest_action_*` columns are the related bill's latest action as of this bill's last update and can lag `bills` for that bill. The source occasionally repeats an identical relationship, so the rows have no unique key.
tables.name: bill_related_bills

tables.comment: Amendments offered to a bill, one row per amendment, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `amendment_type` is SAMDT (Senate) or HAMDT (House); `amendment_number` is unique within (congress, amendment_type). Sponsor columns hold a member's bioguide ID and name; when a committee sponsored the amendment (e.g. the Rules Committee) only `sponsor_name` is set. `amended_amendment_*` is set when the amendment amends another amendment. `purpose` and `description` are usually NULL. `action_count` and `cosponsor_count` count the amendment's own actions and cosponsors, which are the rows of bill_amendment_actions and bill_amendment_cosponsors; roll-call votes on amendment actions are in bill_recorded_votes.
tables.name: bill_amendments

tables.comment: Every recorded action on every amendment in `bill_amendments`, one row per action, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML (introduction, submission, agreed to, not agreed to, withdrawn, ...). Join to `bill_amendments` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number, amendment_type, amendment_number). There is no sequence number: the source does not list amendment actions in date order. Roll-call votes on amendment actions are in bill_recorded_votes. `action_type` values seen: Floor, Committee, IntroReferral, ResolvingDifferences, NotUsed.
tables.name: bill_amendment_actions

tables.comment: Cosponsors of the amendments in `bill_amendments`, one row per (amendment, cosponsor), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. Only Senate amendments (SAMDT) carry cosponsors in the source; House amendments (HAMDT) have none. Join to `bill_amendments` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number, amendment_type, amendment_number) and to officials.members on `bioguide_id`. `withdrawn_date` is set when a cosponsor later withdrew.
tables.name: bill_amendment_cosponsors

tables.comment: The committee named on a bill action, one row per (action, committee), from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML — e.g. the action "Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance." names ssfi00. Join to `bill_actions` on (congress, bill_type, bill_number, action_seq) and to `bill_committees` on committee_system_code. Only actions that involve a committee have a row here.
tables.name: bill_action_committees

tables.comment: Roll-call votes recorded against a bill or one of its amendments, one row per vote, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `url` is the House Clerk or Senate roll-call XML that holds the member-by-member result. A vote on an amendment has `amendment_type` and `amendment_number` set; a vote on the bill itself has them NULL. `action_date` and `action_text` are those of the bill or amendment action that recorded the vote (for example "Passed/agreed to in House: On passage Passed by the Yeas and Nays: 220 - 213"). `full_action_name` (e.g. "Passage of a Measure") appears only on votes listed directly on the bill in a few older files, which then have NULL action fields. One roll call can be cited by several actions on the same bill, so there is one row per citation and no unique key.
tables.name: bill_recorded_votes

tables.comment: Every title recorded for a bill, one row per title, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML — the Display Title, the Official Title as Introduced, short titles as introduced, reported or passed, and the official title as amended or enacted. A bill typically has about three. `title_type` is the source category and `title_type_code` its numeric code. `bill_text_version_code` / `bill_text_version_name` say which text version the title belongs to, and `chamber_code` / `chamber_name` (H, S, J) which chamber it applies to; both are NULL on most rows. `bills.title` is the current official title.
tables.name: bill_titles

tables.comment: CRS summaries of a bill, one row per summary version, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `summary_text` is CRS-written HTML. `version_code` numbers the stage the summary covers (00 = as introduced; later codes mark later stages such as passed one chamber or enacted) and `action_description` names it (e.g. "Introduced in Senate", "Passed House without amendment"). CRS writes summaries after introduction and not for every bill, so many bills have none. `summary_name` and `last_summary_update_date` exist only in a few older files.
tables.name: bill_summaries

tables.comment: Congressional Budget Office cost estimates linked to a bill, one row per estimate, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `title` names the estimate and the stage it covers (e.g. "H.R. 3111, Faster FOIA Act of 2010"), `url` is the CBO publication page, and `description` says what version of the bill it covers ("Cost estimate for the bill as reported by ..."); older rows can hold HTML markup there. The same estimate can appear twice, once with mis-encoded characters in the title, exactly as published.
tables.name: bill_cbo_cost_estimates

tables.comment: House and Senate committee reports filed on a bill, one row per report, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML. `citation` is exactly as published (e.g. "H. Rept. 108-753", sometimes with a book suffix such as "H. Rept. 119-106,Book 1"). A report is occasionally cited twice on the same bill, as published.
tables.name: bill_committee_reports

tables.comment: Congress.gov editorial notes attached to a bill, from the same GovInfo Bill Status XML — for example "For further action, see H.R.366, which became Public Law 112-1". One row per (note, link); a note with no links has one row with NULL `link_name` and `link_url`. `note_text` can contain HTML anchors.
tables.name: bill_notes

tables.comment: Every case decided by the U.S. Supreme Court and printed in the bound United States Reports on GovInfo: volumes 2 through 583, Court terms 1781 through 2017, about 30,800 cases. One row per case, partitioned by `year`, the term in which the volume's cases were decided (the first year of GovInfo's courtTerm; the earliest reporters span several years and count under their first). Terms from 2018 are in scotus_slip_opinions; scotus_cases combines the two. Outcome columns (`disposition`, `party_winning`, `votes_majority`, `votes_minority`, `chief_justice`, `opinion_writer`, `case_origin`, `cert_reason`, `scdb_issue_areas` and the rest of GovInfo's curated fields) come from GovInfo's MODS record, which takes them from the Supreme Court Database, and are present for volumes through 582 only; volume 583 (term 2017) has none, so `disposition` is derived from the opinion text and `disposition_source` says which. `disposition` uses one vocabulary either way: Affirmed (includes modified), Reversed, Reversed and remanded, Vacated and remanded, Affirmed and reversed (or vacated) in part [and remanded], Dismissed as improvidently granted. Text-derived values agree with the curated ones for about 96% of cases; the exceptions are how a remand is coded. `docket_numbers` are the Court's docket numbers read from the opinion (a consolidated case lists every docket whose number the text gives), not the SCDB-format `govinfo_docket_id`. `opinion_text` is the full text of the opinion PDF as extracted, in which the "fi" ligature loses its "i" (e.g. "affrmed", "fnal"). Original-jurisdiction cases have no disposition.
tables.name: scotus_reports_cases

tables.comment: Every lobbying filing made under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, one row per filing: LD-1 registrations (a lobbyist or firm registering to lobby for a client) and LD-2 quarterly activity reports, with their amendments and terminations. `filing_type` says which (decoded in lobbying_filing_types: RR = Registration, Q1 = 1st Quarter Report, and so on). The registrant is the lobbying firm or organization; the client is who it lobbies for (often the same when an organization lobbies for itself). `income` is what a lobbying firm reports receiving from the client and `expenses` is what an organization reports spending on in-house lobbying; each is set on only some filings, as reported (rounded by the filer). `filing_year`/`filing_period` is the reporting period the filing covers. What was lobbied on is in lobbying_activities and the people involved in lobbying_activity_lobbyists. Registrant contact names and telephone numbers and the name of whoever posted a filing are deliberately not carried. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_filings

tables.comment: What each filing says was lobbied on, one row per lobbying activity within a filing (usually one to a handful, one per general issue area). `general_issue_code` is one of the 79 issue areas in lobbying_issue_codes (e.g. DEF = Defense, HCR = Health Issues). `description` is the filer's free-text statement of the specific issues, and is where particular bills, regulations and programs are named (for example "H.R. 1" or "FY26 defense appropriations") — there is no structured bill identifier, so matching to the bill_* tables means reading that text. `activity_seq` numbers the activities within the filing from 1 in the order the API lists them. Join to lobbying_filings on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_activities

tables.comment: The individual lobbyists named on each lobbying activity, one row per (activity, lobbyist). `covered_position` is any covered executive or legislative branch position the lobbyist held in the previous 20 years, as the filer wrote it (e.g. "Principal", "National President"); `is_new` is true when the lobbyist was added on this filing. `lobbyist_id` joins to the lobbyists registry. Join to lobbying_activities on (filing_uuid, activity_seq). Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_activity_lobbyists

tables.comment: The federal bodies each lobbying activity contacted, one row per (activity, government entity): House of Representatives, Senate, and executive agencies such as "Army, Dept of (Other)". `government_entity_id` decodes in lobbying_government_entity_codes. Join to lobbying_activities on (filing_uuid, activity_seq). Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_activity_government_entities

tables.comment: Foreign entities disclosed on a filing because they own or control the client or contribute to the lobbying, one row per (filing, entity). `ownership_percentage` is the share the entity holds in the client and `contribution` the amount it contributed toward the lobbying. Join to lobbying_filings on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_foreign_entities

tables.comment: Organizations affiliated with the client that take part in planning, supervising or controlling its lobbying, one row per (filing, organization). Join to lobbying_filings on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_affiliated_organizations

tables.comment: Convictions of lobbyists disclosed on a filing, one row per (filing, disclosure): the lobbyist, the date and a free-text description. Rare (roughly one filing in a thousand). Join to lobbying_filings on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_conviction_disclosures

tables.comment: Semiannual reports of political contributions filed by registrants and by individual lobbyists (form LD-203), one row per report: the Mid-Year Report (period Jan 1 - Jun 30, `filing_period` mid_year) and the Year-End Report (Jul 1 - Dec 31, year_end). `filer_type` is `lobbyist` when an individual files (the lobbyist_* columns are then set) or `organization` when a registrant files (they are NULL). `no_contributions` is true when the filer certifies it made none. The individual contributions are in lobbying_contribution_items and any PACs the filer controls in lobbying_contribution_pacs. The report's own address is not carried — for an individual it is a home address — only the filer's state and country. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_contribution_reports

tables.comment: The individual contributions listed on LD-203 reports, one row per item: who gave (`contributor_name`, often SELF for an individual lobbyist), who received it (`payee_name`, typically a campaign committee or PAC) and in whose honor (`honoree_name`). `contribution_type` is feca (contribution to a federal candidate, committee or party), he (honorary expenses) and so on, decoded in lobbying_contribution_item_types. Join to lobbying_contribution_reports on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_contribution_items

tables.comment: Political action committees that a registrant or lobbyist reports controlling, one row per (report, PAC) — the API gives only the PAC's name. Join to lobbying_contribution_reports on filing_uuid. Partitioned by `year` and `quarter`: the calendar quarter in which the filing was POSTED (Eastern time), not the period it reports on. A filing keeps its posting date, so a past partition never changes, and an amendment is a new filing in a later partition. The current quarter is re-read on each daily run. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_contribution_pacs

tables.comment: The registry of lobbyists on LDA.gov: every individual who has been listed as a lobbyist on a registration or report (about 88,800 records), one row per lobbyist record with the registrant (lobbying firm or organization) it is filed under. `lobbyist_id` is the same ID used in lobbying_activity_lobbyists and lobbying_conviction_disclosures. This is the full list as of the last monthly refresh, replaced wholesale each month, not a history. Registrant contact names and telephone numbers are deliberately not carried. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbyists

tables.comment: Every registrant on LDA.gov (about 17,500): the lobbying firms and the organizations that lobby for themselves, one row per registrant, replaced wholesale each month. `registrant_id` is the ID used across every lobbying_* table. Contact names and telephone numbers are deliberately not carried. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_registrants

tables.comment: Every client on LDA.gov (about 136,700 records), one row per client record with the registrant that represents it, replaced wholesale each month. `client_id` is the ID used in lobbying_filings. `self_select` is true when the client is the registrant itself, and `government_entity` when the client is a government body. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_clients

tables.comment: The 79 general issue area codes a lobbying activity is filed under (ACC = Accounting, DEF = Defense, HCR = Health Issues, ...). Decodes lobbying_activities.general_issue_code. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_issue_codes

tables.comment: The 257 federal bodies a lobbying activity can report contacting: the House, the Senate and executive agencies. Decodes lobbying_activity_government_entities.government_entity_id. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_government_entity_codes

tables.comment: The 50 filing type codes (RR = Registration, RA = Registration - Amendment, Q1 = 1st Quarter Report, MM = Mid-Year Report, ...) with their variants for amendments and terminations. Decodes filing_type on lobbying_filings and lobbying_contribution_reports. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_filing_types

tables.comment: The five contribution type codes on an LD-203 item (feca = FECA, he = Honorary Expenses, ...). Decodes lobbying_contribution_items.contribution_type. Source: LDA.gov (Senate Office of Public Records). The Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after they have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
tables.name: lobbying_contribution_item_types

tables.comment: Every opinion of the U.S. Supreme Court in the "Opinions of the Court" listing on supremecourt.gov, Court terms 2017 to the current term: the cases the bound volumes in scotus_reports_cases do not cover (term 2017's opinions before March 21, 2018 are in volume 583 there). One row per case, partitioned by `year`, the term (October of `year` to the following summer). `holding_summary` is the Court's own one-line statement of the holding from the listing. `docket_numbers` are read from the opinion (a consolidated case lists every docket its footnote numbers; `listing_docket` is the one the listing gives). `disposition` is derived from the opinion's syllabus, so `disposition_source` is always opinion_text; it uses the vocabulary of scotus_reports_cases (Affirmed (includes modified), Reversed, Reversed and remanded, Vacated and remanded, Affirmed and reversed (or vacated) in part [and remanded], Dismissed as improvidently granted) and can also be Reversed in part and remanded, Reversed in part, vacated in part, and remanded, Vacated in part and remanded or Reversed in part and remanded in part where the Court affirmed no part, or Application granted / Application denied for an order on an emergency application (a docket such as 24A884). It is null for an original-jurisdiction decree. `us_citation` is null while the listing shows only a volume and print part (609/2) and has no page yet. `opinion_text` is the full text as extracted from the PDF, in which the "fi" ligature loses its "i" (e.g. "affrmed", "fnal"). `author_initials` is PC for a per curiam and otherwise the justice's initials as the listing prints them.
tables.name: scotus_slip_opinions

tables.comment: The Supreme Court docket of each case it decided in Court terms 2017 to the current term (the same cases as scotus_slip_opinions): one row per docket, partitioned by `year`, the term the case was decided in. Header fields are the docket's own — title, when it was docketed, the court below and its case numbers and decision date, any application it is linked with, and the Questions Presented. `granted_date`, `argued_date` and `judgment_issued_date` are the dates of the docket entries "Petition GRANTED", "Argued." and "Judgment Issued." and are null where the docket has none (a summary reversal is not argued; a docket in which the Court's own entry is misspelt has no judgment date). `entry_count` and `document_count` count the docket's entries and the filings linked from them; the entries are in scotus_docket_entries. Join to scotus_slip_opinions on `docket_number` = `listing_docket`. Not included: dockets of cases decided before term 2017 (the docket pages before 2016 use an older layout that is not read), original-jurisdiction cases (their page address cannot be derived from the listing), and, for a consolidated case, the companion dockets — only the lead docket the listing names is fetched. No petitions the Court declined to hear are here.
tables.name: scotus_dockets

tables.comment: Every entry in the "Proceedings and Orders" of the dockets in scotus_dockets, one row per entry in the order the docket lists them (`sequence` from 1), partitioned by `year`, the term the case was decided in. Extensions of time, briefs including those of amici, the distribution of the petition for conference, the grant, the argument and the judgment all appear here as the Court's own text in `entry_text`, with the filings linked from the entry in `document_labels` and `document_urls` (parallel lists). Join to scotus_dockets on `docket_number`. Same coverage as scotus_dockets: decided cases from term 2017, lead docket of a consolidated case, no original-jurisdiction cases.
tables.name: scotus_docket_entries

tables.comment: House members' (and their spouses' and dependent children's) STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports — stock, option and fund trades disclosed within 30-45 days of the transaction, from the Clerk of the House's own bulk financial-disclosure system. Not annual financial disclosures (outside income, asset/liability ranges, gifts) and not the Senate's parallel eFD filings — see the column-level and class-level comments for why. `filing_id` groups the one or more transaction rows a single PTR lists; `row_seq` (from 1) is their order in the filing. `owner_code` is blank for the member's own holding, SP for a spouse, JT for a joint holding, DC for a dependent child. `asset_type_code` is the source's own abbreviation (ST, OP, OT, ...; see https://fd.house.gov/reference/asset-type-codes.aspx) with `ticker` parsed out of it separately when the source prints one; a private holding, fund or real property has no ticker. `asset_type_code` is null for 2015-2017 filings — that PTR template predates the asset-type-code column entirely (see member_stock_transactions_year_range comment). `amount_min`/`amount_max` are the disclosed bracket's bounds in dollars (`amount_max` null for the open-ended top bracket); the source never discloses an exact amount. Coverage starts in 2015, the earliest year the source's own filing-type coding distinguishes PTRs from other disclosure types; filings before 2015 exist but aren't identifiable as PTRs in the index.
tables.name: member_stock_transactions

officials.comment: Federally elected and federally appointed officeholders. `members` covers every person who has served in the House or Senate (Congress.gov API, the modernized successor to the Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress). `nominations` covers PAS nominations — the live pipeline of Senate-confirmed appointed officials, from receipt through committee action to confirmation/withdrawal. `federal_judges` covers every Article III judge ever commissioned, including appointing president and confirmation history, from the Federal Judicial Center's own biographical database. `committees` and `committee_membership` cover House/Senate/Joint committee structure, jurisdiction, and current rosters — the one table pair in this schema sourced from a community-maintained aggregator (unitedstates/congress-legislators) rather than a government system of record directly, because no official source exposes committee membership or jurisdiction in structured form; see the header comment above.

tables.comment: Every House/Senate member per Congress they served, from the Congress.gov API per-Congress member list endpoint (the modernized Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress). One row per (bioguide_id, congress) pair — a member serving multiple congresses has multiple rows. `terms_json` is the member's full chamber service history (all congresses, not just this row's), as a JSON array of {chamber, start_year, end_year}. `party_name` is the party held in this row's Congress (from the detail endpoint's partyHistory; a mid-Congress switch resolves to the party held when that Congress ended), so a party switcher's rows differ by Congress. Chamber is not a column: `district` is null for senators and non-null (0 = at-large) for House members. A Congress holds more rows than seats because mid-Congress replacements each get a row, so party control is not a plain COUNT. `state_name` and `district` are as reported by the per-Congress list endpoint. Coverage is bounded by `congress_range` (see dimension_values comment) — not full 1789-present history by default. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name (full name; geo.states is a year-vintaged boundary snapshot and not a valid FK target — see constraints below). Territorial delegates (Puerto Rico, Guam, etc.) won't resolve against state_ref, which covers 50 states + DC only.
tables.name: members

tables.comment: Presidential nominations requiring Senate confirmation (PAS), from the Congress.gov API nomination endpoint — this IS the appointed-officials pipeline: received -> committee referral -> confirmed/withdrawn/returned. Verified against a live keyed response (2026-08-01): `organization` is a real top-level field, not an N+1-only one as originally assumed. `description` is populated for individually -named nominees but is empty for isList=true batch nominations (e.g. Foreign Service class promotions covering many officers at once) — the detail endpoint's `isList` flag itself is not fetched here, so an empty description is the only MVP signal that a row is a class nomination rather than a named appointee. `latest_action_text` is the best single field for current status (e.g. "Confirmed by the Senate by Voice Vote", "Nomination Withdrawn").
tables.name: nominations

tables.comment: Every Article III federal judge ever commissioned, from the Federal Judicial Center's own Biographical Directory of Article III Federal Judges export. Verified against a live download (2026-08-01): the real CSV is 201 columns wide — up to 6 repeating groups of ~33 court/appointment columns each (a judge elevated District -> Circuit -> retired-then-recalled etc. gets multiple groups), plus separate "Other Federal Judicial Service", "School"/"Degree", and free-text career columns. This table maps a curated 12-of-33 fields per group (the appointment-identity and confirmation-timeline columns) and drops the education/career/committee-vote detail for MVP scope — not a parsing limitation, a deliberate cut. Ingested as one row per judge (one source, minimal reshape); a future `federal_judgeships` view could UNION ALL the 6 groups into one row per appointment if downstream queries need that grain.
tables.name: federal_judges

tables.comment: House, Senate, and Joint standing/select committees and their subcommittees, from the unitedstates/congress-legislators project's committees-current.yaml — a CC0-licensed, near-continuously-updated mirror of official House/Senate committee pages. The one community-aggregator source in this schema: verified live that the Congress.gov API's /v3/committee endpoint carries no jurisdiction text and no member roster (see the schema header). One row per full committee and one row per subcommittee, linked via parent_committee_id; committee_id is the join key into committee_membership.
tables.name: committees

tables.comment: Current committee/subcommittee rosters, from the unitedstates/congress-legislators project's committee-membership-current.yaml. One row per (committee, member) assignment for the sitting Congress. committee_id joins to committees.committee_id; bioguide_id joins to members.bioguide_id — this file has no congress number of its own (it is always the current roster), so join against the member's most recent congress rather than a specific one (see current_members).
tables.name: committee_membership

tables.comment: Electoral College vote allocation by state, for President and Vice President, from the National Archives (NARA) official per-election results page (archives.gov/electoral-college/{year}) — the government's own record of the Electoral College outcome, not a poll or projection. One row per (year, state, office, candidate). Verified stable across 200 years of live pages (1824, 1876, 1960, 1980, 2000, 2020, 2024): each page has a state-by-state table whose "For President"/"For Vice-President" header groups carry a colspan equal to however many candidates received at least one elector that year — parsed dynamically, not a fixed column count. `candidate_party` is populated only for the winner and the top losing candidate (the only two NARA names on the page's own summary block); other candidates' party is null — NARA's per-election page does not state it for anyone else, including write-in/faithless-elector recipients. Coverage defaults to 1976-2024 (presidential_year_range) — see that dimension's comment for why 1789 isn't the floor. Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name (same caveat as members: DC has 3 electoral votes since the 23rd Amendment but is not itself a state, so 3-elector DC rows will not resolve against a strict state_ref join in years before 1961 if the range is widened).
tables.name: electoral_college_votes

tables.comment: Popular vote totals by state and candidate for the presidential general election, from the FEC's official post-election results workbook (fec.gov, "{year} Presidential General Election Results", published as XLSX). Richer than electoral_college_votes for the years it covers — actual vote counts, not just elector allocation — but coverage is NOT full-history: FEC only publishes this specific XLSX format for recent cycles (confirmed: 2024; unconfirmed further back — the source page lists only PDF, not XLSX, for cycles further back at the time this table was built, 2026-08-02). No predictable per-year URL exists (each year's file lives behind an opaque numeric document ID), so this transformer discovers the URL per year by scraping FEC's static results-and-voting-information listing page rather than templating a URL directly — a year with no matching link on that page yields zero rows for this table, not an error; check the ETL log for "no results link found" to distinguish "not published this way" from a real failure. One row per (year, state, candidate). Cross-references geo.state_ref via state_name.
tables.name: presidential_election_results

patents.comment: USPTO patent grant and trademark application data from PatentsView bulk downloads and USPTO trademark bulk CSV. Patent tables are year-partitioned by grant_year (1976+). Trademark tables are year-partitioned by application_year. Claims and summaries include vector embedding columns (FLOAT[]) populated at ingestion time via batched embedding calls. Full-dump files are cached locally under GOVDATA_CACHE_DIR/patents/ with a quarterly TTL to avoid re-downloading on every year invocation.

tables.comment: One row per granted patent (patent_type utility or plant by default; design patents excluded unless PATENTS_INCLUDE_DESIGN=true), with patent_date, patent_title, num_claims, wipo_kind, and a withdrawn flag. Faithful recreation of g_patent.tsv, no joins, year-partitioned by grant_year starting from GOVDATA_START_YEAR (nominally 2010, but the configured/actual floor can drift — check observedCoverage below for the real minYear rather than assuming it matches the default) — narrower than the six full-dump snapshot tables (patent_assignees, patent_inventors, patent_cpc_classes, patent_abstracts, patent_applications, patent_figures), which cover all patents back to 1976 with no year cutoff. Abstract, filing date, and figure counts live in those tables, joined on patent_id at query time.
tables.name: patent_grants

tables.comment: To reach a patent assignee FROM a company rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on patents_assignee_id = assignee_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so a firm's SEC CIK and its patent assignee id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching assignee_organization as text finds the wrong entities and misses subsidiaries filing under unrelated names. Faithful recreation of g_assignee_disambiguated.tsv — one row per patent-assignee combination (assignee_organization or first/last name, assignee_type, assignee_sequence), keyed by patent_id, no joins and no year. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row). location_id is the foreign key into patent_locations for geography.
tables.name: patent_assignees

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_inventor_disambiguated.tsv (~8 GB uncompressed) — one row per patent-inventor combination, keyed by patent_id, with an inferred gender_code useful for diversity analysis. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row). location_id is the foreign key into patent_locations for geography.
tables.name: patent_inventors

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_cpc_current.tsv — one row per patent-CPC code combination (cpc_section, cpc_class, cpc_subclass, cpc_group, cpc_type), keyed by patent_id; CPC is the primary technology taxonomy for patent analysis. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row).
tables.name: patent_cpc_classes

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_patent_abstract.tsv — one row per patent abstract, keyed by patent_id. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row).
tables.name: patent_abstracts

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_application.tsv — one row per application record (filing_date, patent_application_type), keyed by patent_id. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row).
tables.name: patent_applications

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_figures.tsv — one row per patent figure/sheet count record (num_figures, num_sheets), keyed by patent_id. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot covering all patents back to 1976 (broader than patent_grants, which only materializes GOVDATA_START_YEAR+/2010+, so older patent_ids here have no patent_grants row).
tables.name: patent_figures

tables.comment: Faithful recreation of g_location_disambiguated.tsv — one row per disambiguated location (state_fips, county_fips, country_code, latitude, longitude), keyed by location_id. FK target for patent_inventors.location_id and patent_assignees.location_id. Loaded once per quarter as a full snapshot.
tables.name: patent_locations

tables.comment: One row per patent claim. Claims define the legal scope of the patent — the most analytically useful text component. Per-year source files: g_claims_{year}.tsv.zip from the PatentsView claims/ subdirectory. The embedding column is populated at ingestion time via batched embedding calls. For dependent claims, the transformer prepends the parent independent claim text before embedding to capture full legal scope.
tables.name: patent_claims

tables.comment: One row per patent. Brief summary section text from the patent specification. More concise than the full description; covers key aspects and distinguishing features over prior art. Per-year source files: g_brf_sum_text_{year}.tsv.zip from the PatentsView brief-summary-text/ subdirectory. The embedding column is populated at ingestion time.
tables.name: patent_summaries

tables.comment: Faithful landing of USPTO TRCFECO2 case_file.csv — one row per trademark application (serial_no), all 79 source columns verbatim. Year-partitioned by application filing year.
tables.name: trademark_case_file

tables.comment: Faithful landing of USPTO TRCFECO2 owner.csv — applicant/owner identity, one row per (serial_no, own_seq). own_addr_state_cd is a 2-letter code, not FIPS — join geo.state_ref. To reach a trademark owner's cross-schema identity FROM another schema rather than by name, join ref.canonical_org_entity on patents_trademark_owner_id = own_id — that table carries one foreign key per source, so the owner's LEI/SEC CIK and its own_id sit in the same row and the join is exact. Matching own_name as text finds the wrong entities and misses owners filing under a differently-worded name.
tables.name: trademark_owner

tables.comment: Faithful landing of USPTO TRCFECO2 classification.csv — US class + first-use dates + status, one row per (serial_no, class_id).
tables.name: trademark_classification

tables.comment: Faithful landing of USPTO TRCFECO2 intl_class.csv — international (Nice) class codes, one row per (serial_no, intl_class_cd).
tables.name: trademark_intl_class

tables.comment: Faithful landing of USPTO TRCFECO2 statement.csv — goods/services and other statement text, one row per (serial_no, statement_type_cd).
tables.name: trademark_statement

ref.comment: Reference and cross-referencing tables for financial entity identification. Links SEC CIK identifiers to GLEIF LEI codes and OpenFIGI instrument identifiers. Enables cross-system entity resolution for financial data analysis.

tables.comment: GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) records from the Global LEI Foundation golden copy CSV — entity registration details, jurisdiction, legal form, HQ/registered addresses, and registration authority links. The registration_authority_entity_id field contains the SEC CIK number for entities registered with RA000665 (SEC EDGAR); most other registration authorities carry that jurisdiction's own business-registry number instead (e.g. RA000602, Delaware Division of Corporations), so this column is only a CIK when registration_authority_id is actually RA000665 — see gleif_cik_mapping, which applies that filter. Append-only changelog: one row per LEI per publish in which it changed, with last_update as the history axis; use the current_gleif_entities view for the latest row per LEI. Source: GLEIF Golden Copy (goldencopy.gleif.org).
tables.name: gleif_entities

tables.comment: Bridge table mapping GLEIF LEI codes to SEC CIK numbers (lei, cik, legal_name, entity_status). Derived from the GLEIF golden copy CSV filtered where registration_authority_id = 'RA000665' (SEC EDGAR). That authority ID covers both real filer CIKs and SEC fund-series identifiers (e.g. "S000005113") registered with SEC but not themselves filers — a validator drops any non-numeric cik value, since a series ID never matches a real CIK downstream. Current snapshot only, overwritten each run — unlike gleif_entities, which keeps an append-only change history. Provides fast LEI <-> CIK lookups without scanning the full GLEIF dataset. entity_org_bridge.sec_cik (EIN-path matches) joins here on cik = sec_cik to reach the LEI — the exact bridge for that column; do not name-match its org against gleif_entities.legal_name.
tables.name: gleif_cik_mapping

tables.comment: GLEIF Level 2 relationship records — the LEI-to-LEI edges that LEI-CDF (gleif_entities) does not carry. One row per directed relationship. Both endpoints are always LEIs, so the table self-joins to gleif_entities on either side and, through gleif_cik_mapping, resolves to SEC CIKs. relationship_type values (2026-07-31 publish, 482,849 rows): IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY (126,021) and IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY (132,196) are the two levels of the ownership hierarchy; IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY (148,576), IS_SUBFUND_OF (72,731), IS_FEEDER_TO (1,386) are fund structures; IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF (1,939) is branch registration. In every type start_node_id is the subordinate entity and end_node_id is the superior one — but only consolidation means ownership. A fund commonly carries a manager AND an umbrella (59,419 entities; the two are different entities in 60,266 of 60,370 cases): two distinct relations, not two parents. GLEIF flattens the ownership chain to two attested levels and never publishes the intermediate one, so IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY is largely derivable — walking the direct chain reaches the declared ultimate for 113,860 of the 118,627 entities that report both. It is kept because it is REPORTED, not computed: 13,569 entities declare an ultimate with no direct edge to walk from, and 4,765 chains break at an intermediate holding company that has no LEI. Dropping it loses those ~18k attestations. Only entities that report a relationship to GLEIF appear here — an absent edge means "not reported", which the REPEX (reporting exception) publish explains and this table does not carry. Source: GLEIF Golden Copy RR (goldencopy.gleif.org).
tables.name: gleif_relationships

tables.comment: SEC EDGAR company ticker mapping: cik, ticker, title (registered company name), and as_of (the UTC ingest date). ~10,000 active US exchange-listed companies, sourced from the SEC EDGAR company_tickers.json file (updated daily). Each run stamps a fresh as_of snapshot, so grouping by as_of recovers ticker/name history over time. Feeds the ticker dimension for figi_instruments — enables the full chain LEI → CIK → ticker → FIGI within the ref schema with no dependency on other schemas. Source: https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json
tables.name: sec_company_tickers

tables.comment: Financial instrument identifiers from OpenFIGI. Maps tickers to FIGI codes with exchange, market sector, and security type information. Requires an OpenFIGI API key (set OPENFIGI_API_KEY environment variable). Rate limited to 25 requests/minute with API key, 5 requests/minute without.
tables.name: figi_instruments

tables.comment: Country identity crosswalk: one row per country carrying the Census 4-digit trade code, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2/alpha-3/numeric, FIPS 10-4, a name-based BEA area key, plus M49 region/subregion/continent and ISO 4217 currency. Lets the Census-coded trade tables (econ.trade_by_state / trade_exports / trade_imports), the ISO-3-coded econ.world_indicators, and the name-keyed BEA tables (econ.ita_data / fdi_*) all join to a single reference. Sources: Census Schedule C country list (live, freshness-gated) + a bundled ISO spine derived from DataHub datasets/country-codes (public domain).
tables.name: countries

tables.comment: NAICS 2022 industry classification: one row per 2-to-6-digit code with its title and hierarchy level (2=sector, 3=subsector, 4=industry group, 5=NAICS industry, 6=national industry).
